name: Achari chicken
label: ACHARI
portion: 1/7 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken thighs, boneless skinless (cuisses de poulet désossées) | 1.25 kg | 4 cm pieces |
| Oil | 40 ml | |
| **Pickle seeds:** fennel seeds (habbet hlawa / fenouil), nigella (sanouj), cumin seeds (kammoun), fenugreek seeds (helba) | 2 tsp, 1 tsp, 1 tsp, 1 tsp | |
| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~250 g) | finely chopped |
| Garlic (thoum) | 4 cloves (20 g) | crushed |
| Fresh ginger (skinjbir) | 15 g | grated |
| Tomatoes (tmatem) | 2 large (~300 g) | finely chopped |
| Ground coriander | 1 tsp | |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tsp | instead of red chilli powder |
| Turmeric (kourkoum) | ¾ tsp | |
| Salt | 2 tsp, to taste | |
| Water | 100 ml | |
| Plain yogurt (yaourt nature) | 1 pot (120 g) | whisked, at room temperature |
| Lemon juice (citron) | 2 tbsp (30 ml) | |
| Fresh coriander (kosbor) and a little ginger | small handful + 5 g | chopped / cut into thin matchsticks |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, medium-high:** heat the oil in a heavy pot, add all the pickle seeds and let them sizzle for **15–20 s** (the fenugreek should go just a shade darker, not brown). Straight away, add the onion.
2. Fry the onion for **10–12 min** until lightly golden; splash in 2 tbsp water if it catches. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min**.
3. Add the chicken with ½ tsp salt and stir-fry for **2–3 min**, until it's white on the outside.
4. Add the tomatoes, coriander, paprika, turmeric and the rest of the salt. Cook for **2–3 min** until the tomatoes soften, then add the water and bring to a boil.
5. **Lid on, low-medium, 13–15 min**, stirring once, until the chicken is white all the way through.
6. Lid off, heat up to high for **3–4 min** to cook off the excess liquid; the chicken turns glossy and the oil starts to separate.
7. Heat down to low. Stir in the whisked yogurt a spoonful at a time (stirring stops it splitting) and cook gently for **2–3 min**. **Off the heat**, add the lemon juice, then the coriander and ginger matchsticks. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Nutrition (calculated)
sections.content:
**Assembly check:** one labeled serving of this dish + one [rice serving](../../recipes/riz.md) + one [chakchouka serving](../../recipes/chakchouka.md) ≈ **643 kcal, 42.9 g protein**. A labeled serving may span several cubes.

label: ALOO GOBI

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Biggest pot (or split between two on two burners), medium heat:** oil and onions for **4–5 min**, until soft and translucent.
2. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min**, then the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and garam masala for 30–60 s, stirring so they don't burn.
3. Add the tomatoes and cook **5 min**, stirring, until they break down into a thick gravy.
4. Add the potatoes, stock and salt, stir, bring to a lively simmer, then lid on at a gentle simmer for **7 min**.
5. Add the cauliflower and stir well (a splash more water if it's dry). Lid on, **10–12 min**, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are cooked through and the cauliflower is just tender.
6. Lid off for **2–3 min** to dry off any liquid. Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

name: American goulash (beef macaroni)
label: US GOULASH
portion: 1/6 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: vegetable cubes; already contains its starch

sections.title: Ingredients (6 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Oil | 2 tsp (10 g) | |
| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~200 g) | finely chopped |
| Green pepper (felfel hlou / poivron vert) | 1 large (~200 g) | 1 cm dice |
| Beef mince, lean (viande hachée maigre) | 750 g | |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux), dried oregano, basil | 1 tbsp, 1 tsp, 1 tsp | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 40 g (1½ tbsp) | |
| Ripe tomatoes (tmatem) | ~800 g | grated, skins thrown away (or 2 × 400 g cans) |
| Ketchup | 3 tbsp (45 g) | |
| Bay leaves (laurier) | 2 | |
| Beef stock cube | 1 | dissolved in 900 ml hot water |
| Macaroni (coudes / macaroni) | 400 g | |
| Sweetcorn, canned (maïs doux) | 1 can (~285 g drained) | drained |
| Evaporated milk, unsweetened (lait concentré non sucré) | 160 g | |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 80 g | grated |
| Salt, black pepper (felfel k'hal) | 1 tsp, ½ tsp | taste at the end; the stock is salty |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- If lait concentré non sucré is unavailable, gently reduce **2 ml whole milk to 1 ml** needed, then measure the reduced amount before use. Sweetened condensed milk is unsuitable for this savoury dish.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Big pot, medium heat:** oil, onion, green pepper and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft with no raw bite.
2. Turn up, add the **beef** and break it up for **6–8 min**, until no pink is left. Add the garlic, paprika, oregano and basil for **1 min** (keep it moving; paprika catches), then the tomato paste for 1 min.
3. Add the grated tomatoes, ketchup, bay and the **900 ml stock**. Bring to the boil and simmer **5 min**.
4. Tip in the **macaroni**, stir, and bring back to a simmer. Lid half on, medium-low, **stirring every 2 min and scraping the bottom**, for **2 min less than the packet says** (usually **8–9 min**). If it gets thick before the pasta is done, add a splash of hot water.
5. Heat off. Fish out the bay, then stir in the corn, evaporated milk and cheese until melted. Taste for salt and pepper.
6. It should look **too saucy**, like a loose macaroni cheese. That's right: the pasta keeps drinking as it cools.

Want it hotter? Harissa on your own bowl at the table, never in the pot.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

label: APPLE CHKN
portion: 1/7 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:

|---|---|---|

| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~250 g) | thinly sliced |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Apple juice (jus de pomme, 100% if you can find it) | 300 ml | |
| Honey (asal / miel) | 50 g (2½ tbsp) | |
| Soy sauce (sauce soja) | 40 ml (2½ tbsp) | |
| Cider vinegar (vinaigre de cidre) | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | |
| Dried rosemary or thyme (romarin / zaâtar) | 1 tsp | |
| Cinnamon (qarfa) | ½ tsp | |
| Black pepper (felfel k'hal) | ½ tsp | |
| Cornflour (maïzena) | 2 tbsp (15 g) | mixed with 3 tbsp cold water |
| Apples, firm (teffah; Golden or Granny) | 2 (~340 g) | peeled, cored, 8 wedges each |
| Butter (beurre) | 15 g | |
| Salt | ½ tsp, to taste | the soy is already salty |

Boneless breast (escalope) works too: about 345 kcal and a different nutritional contribution per serving, but give it only 2½–3 h on low or it goes stringy.

sections.content:

- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Slow cooker:** onion and garlic in the bottom, chicken on top. Whisk the apple juice, honey, soy, vinegar, rosemary, cinnamon and pepper and pour it over. Lid on, **low 4 h** (or high 2½ h). The chicken is done when a piece breaks apart easily and there's no pink inside.
2. **Last 20 min:** turn it to high, stir in the cornflour slurry and leave the lid off so the sauce thickens to a glossy coating.
3. Meanwhile, **burner 1, medium:** melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the apple wedges for **5–6 min**, turning once, until golden at the edges but still holding their shape. Pinch of salt.
4. Fold the apples into the chicken. Taste: a little more vinegar if it's too sweet, a pinch of salt if it's flat.
5. **Pressure cooker instead:** soften the onion on sauté for 3 min, add everything except the cornflour and apples, **high pressure 8 min**, natural release 10 min, then back on sauté with the slurry for 2–3 min until thick. Fry the apples as above.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **A, apple:** grated apple in a bowl, covered, **microwave 4–5 min**, stir, then 1–2 min more uncovered until soft and most of the juice has gone. Cool 10 min.
2. **A, food processor:** oats, raisins and cinnamon until the oats are fine. Add the cooked apple, peanut butter, honey, chia and salt and pulse until it clumps. If it's too wet to roll, add a spoon of oats. Tip into a bowl and chill **30 min** in the fridge.
3. **B, food processor** (no need to wash it): peanuts and pistachios, pulsed into coarse crumbs. Add the dates and raisins and process until sticky, then the oats, honey, chia and salt, and pulse until it holds when squeezed. Chill **30 min**.
4. Mix the flaxseed into batch A. Press both completed mixtures into 60 ml molds, keeping the two flavours separate.


**Cube version:** instead of forming balls or cutting bars, press the completed mixtures into 60 ml molds, including their chocolate or nut layers. Keep any different flavours separate. Never add uncooked flour; the oat and nut ingredients here are ready to eat.

2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Frying pan on a burner, medium:** oil and onion with a pinch of salt for **8 min** until soft and golden. Garlic for 1 min.
2. Into the slow cooker: the onion and garlic, jam, ketchup, mayonnaise, dried apricots, soy, vinegar, paprika, pepper and stock. Stir to mix, then add the thighs and turn to coat.
3. **Lid on, low 4 h** (or high 2½ h), until the chicken is tender and 74 °C in the thickest thigh.
4. Lift the thighs onto a board and cut into 3–4 cm chunks. Set the cooker to **high**, stir in the cornflour slurry and cook **lid off for 15 min**, stirring once, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
5. Chicken back in and stir. Taste: a dash more vinegar if it's too sweet, salt if flat.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté** (or a heavy pot on medium-high): 20 ml oil and the onions for **5 min**, until soft. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 min.
2. Add the beef and stir for **3 min**, until no longer red on the outside. Add the soy, honey, vinegar, star anise, cinnamon, pepper, stock cube and **1.2 L water**. Scrape the bottom well so nothing is stuck (a stuck base trips the burn warning).
3. **Lid on, high pressure 15 min**, then natural release for 10 min. The beef should break when pressed with a spoon; if it doesn't, give it 5 min more. Pot instead: lid on, simmer **1 h 15 min**.
4. **8 L pot, big burner:** tip in the beef and broth with the other **1 L water** and bring to a simmer. Add the carrots and mushrooms for **10 min**, then the cabbage for **3 min**. Fish out the star anise and cinnamon. Taste: a splash more soy if it needs salt, a few drops of vinegar if it tastes flat.
5. **Meanwhile, second burner:** a big pot of salted water at a rolling boil. Cook the noodles for **1 min less than the packet says** (usually 3 min), drain, rinse under cold water until cool, and toss with 1 tsp oil so they don't stick.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven grill on high**, shelf near the top. Lay the eggplants on foil-lined trays and grill **35–45 min**, turning every 10–15 min, until the skin is blackened all over and they've collapsed and are completely soft inside. (For extra smokiness, char 1–2 at a time directly over a gas burner first.)

5. Add the mashed eggplant and fry it slowly for **15–20 min**, stirring often, until it's a thick, glossy purée with oil shining at the edges (this long fry is where the flavour comes from).
6. Off the heat, stir in the fresh coriander, lemon juice and garam masala. Taste for salt. Cool **30 min**.

| Beef mince, lean (viande hachée maigre) | 750 g | |
| Garlic (thoum) | 1 whole head (~40 g) | peeled, finely chopped |
| Green pepper (felfel hlou / poivron vert) | 1 large (~180 g) | 1 cm dice |
| Mushrooms (champignons de Paris) | 250 g | sliced |
| Ripe tomatoes (tmatem) | ~1 kg | grated, skins thrown away (or 2 × 400 g cans + 200 ml passata) |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 40 g (1½ tbsp) | |
| Dried oregano, basil, sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tsp each | |
| Sugar | 1 tsp | |
| Salt, black pepper (felfel k'hal) | 1½ tsp, ½ tsp | |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 100 g | grated |

Pizza-style variant (from the pizza casserole): swap 150 g of the beef for diced *cachir* and add an extra teaspoon of oregano.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1:** big pot of salted water on to boil.
2. **Burner 2, wide pot, medium heat:** oil and onion with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min**, until soft with no raw bite. Turn up, add the **beef** and break it up for **5 min**.
3. Add the garlic, green pepper and mushrooms and cook **6–8 min**, stirring, until the mushrooms have given up their water and it's cooked off. Keep the heat at medium once the garlic's in; burnt garlic is bitter.
4. Stir in the tomato paste, oregano, basil and paprika for 1 min, then the grated tomatoes, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer with the lid off for **20 min**, until thick.
5. **Burner 1:** when the sauce has about 10 min left, cook the pasta for **3 min less than the packet says** (about 8 min for rigatoni). Scoop out a mugful of the pasta water, then drain.
6. **Oven 200 °C.** Tip the pasta into the sauce with **60 ml of the pasta water** and **half the cheese**, and stir well. It should look **saucier than you'd serve it**: the pasta keeps drinking as it bakes and freezes.
7. Spread it in the oven dish, scatter the rest of the cheese on top and **bake 20 min**, until the cheese has melted and is golden in patches.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Butter a **30 × 40 cm** deep oven tray. Spread in the bread cubes and scatter the apple through them.
2. **Custard:** whisk the milk powder into the milk first (no lumps), then the eggs, sugar, vanilla sugar, 1½ tsp cinnamon, nutmeg, orange zest, salt and 40 g melted butter.
3. Pour it evenly over the bread and press down with a spatula so every cube is wet. **Soak 20–30 min** (fresh bread goes mushy; stale bread drinks it up). Heat the oven to **180 °C** meanwhile.
4. **Topping:** rub the oats, brown sugar, the last ½ tsp cinnamon and 20 g soft butter together with your fingers and scatter over the top.
5. Bake **40–45 min**, until puffed and golden and a knife in the middle comes out with no runny custard.
6. Drizzle the honey over while it's hot. Cool **15 min**, then cut into **15 squares** (3 × 5).

portion: 1/16 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: compatible dessert cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (16 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Very ripe bananas (mouz) | 4 (~480 g peeled) | mashed smooth |
| Flour (farine) | 170 g | |
| Wholemeal flour (farine complète) | 160 g | |
| Baking powder (levure chimique) | 1 sachet (~11 g) | |
| Cinnamon (qarfa) | 1½ tsp | |
| Salt | 1 tsp | |
| Sugar (sucre) | 200 g | |
| Oil | 165 ml (~150 g) | |
| Eggs (œufs) | 3 | |
| Vanilla sugar (sucre vanillé) | 2 sachets (~15 g) | |
| Raisins (zbib), or chocolate chips | 100 g | |
| Brown sugar (cassonade) | 20 g | for the tops |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Épicerie alternatives: white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 175 °C.** Line two 25 cm loaf tins (moules à cake) with parchment.
2. Whisk both flours, the baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
3. In a big bowl, whisk the sugar and oil for **1 min** until pale, then the eggs one at a time, then the mashed banana and vanilla sugar.
4. Stir in the flour mix **just until combined**, then fold in the raisins.
5. Split between the tins, level, and sprinkle with the brown sugar.
6. Bake **45–50 min**, until risen and deep golden and a skewer in the middle comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil for the last 15 min if the tops darken too fast.
7. Rest 10–15 min, then remove from the tins and portion into smaller pieces. Chill promptly on a shallow tray if not ready to mold; do not wait an hour on the counter in a hot kitchen.


**Cube version:** use the completed baked mixture, including any listed glaze, after it has set. Cut into pieces smaller than a mold cavity and press gently into 60 ml freezer molds; use the listed moist fruit/filling to bind crumbs, not raw batter. Pack separate flavours separately. A cake cube is a dessert component; serve it warm with a separately frozen fruit or yogurt component.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **16 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **60 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

name: BBQ drumsticks
label: BBQ PILONS
portion: 1/7 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken drumsticks (pilons) | 21 (~2.1 kg) | 2 deep slashes each, to the bone |
| **Marinade** | | |
| Dijon mustard (moutarde) | 2 tbsp (30 g) | |
| Honey (asal / miel) | 1 tbsp (20 g) | |
| Cider vinegar (vinaigre de cidre) | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | |
| Oil | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Rub: 1 tbsp sweet paprika (paprika doux), 1 tsp sweet smoked paprika (paprika fumé doux), 1 tsp cumin (kammoun), ½ tsp black pepper (felfel k'hal) | ~12 g | |
| Salt | 1½ tsp | |
| **Glaze** | | |
| Ketchup | 150 g | |
| Honey | 2 tbsp (40 g) | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 1 tbsp (20 g) | |
| Cider vinegar | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | |
| Sweet smoked paprika | ½ tsp | |

Drumsticks here run 90–120 g each. If yours are small, make it 24 and give each portion 3–4; the protein holds.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinate:** mix the marinade ingredients with the rub and salt in a big bowl, add the drumsticks and massage it into the slashes. Cover and chill **1–4 h**.
2. **Oven 200 °C** (fan 180 °C). Line 2 trays with parchment. Lay the drumsticks out with a finger's gap between them; touching drumsticks steam instead of browning.
3. **Roast 30 min**, then turn them and swap the trays.
4. **Glaze:** stir the ketchup, honey, tomato paste, vinegar and smoked paprika together. Brush half over the drumsticks and roast **10 min**. Turn, brush on the rest and roast **10 min more**.
5. They're done when the meat pulls back from the bone, the juices run clear and the thickest one reads 74 °C next to the bone. The glaze should be sticky and dark at the edges, not black; if it's catching, move that tray down a shelf.


**Prepare for cubes:** After cooking, remove every bone and piece of cartilage and chop or shred the meat to 1–2 cm. Mix it with the cooked sauce and juices before filling molds; no bones go into a cube. For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- If lait concentré non sucré is unavailable, gently reduce **2 ml whole milk to 1 ml** needed, then measure the reduced amount before use. Sweetened condensed milk is unsuitable for this savoury dish.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir; white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C**, two trays lined with parchment.
2. **Meatballs:** in a big bowl, stir the evaporated milk, oats, eggs, onion, garlic, stock cube, spices, salt and pepper; leave **5 min** for the oats to soften. Add the mince and mix with your hands until even. Roll about **35 balls** (~40 g each) and space them out on the trays.
3. **Bake 18–20 min**, until browned and cooked through (no pink when you cut one open).
4. **Sauce, while they bake:** wide pot on medium-low, everything for the sauce, stirred, for **5 min** until it bubbles and the sugar dissolves. It catches easily, so keep stirring.
5. Add the meatballs and their juices, lid on, and simmer very gently for **10 min**, turning them twice, until glazed. If it's too thick to coat them, add a splash of water.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Mix the rub and massage it all over the beef.
2. **Burner 1, big pan, high:** oil, then brown the beef **3 min a side**. Into the slow cooker.
3. **Same pan, medium:** onions for **6–8 min** until soft and golden, then the garlic for 1 min. Add all the BBQ sauce ingredients and the stock, stir, bring to a bubble, and pour it over the beef.
4. **Lid on, low 8–9 h** (high 4–5 h), until the beef pulls apart with a fork. Pressure cooker instead: steps 2–3 on sauté, then **high pressure 60 min**, natural release 15 min.
5. Lift the beef out and shred it with two forks. If the sauce is thin, boil it in a pot on burner 1 for **5–10 min** until it coats a spoon (slow-cooker sauce always needs this). Beef back into the sauce and stir well. Taste for salt and vinegar.

| Oil | 2 tsp (10 ml) | |
| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~200 g) | finely chopped |
| Garlic (thoum) | 2 cloves (10 g) | crushed |
| **BBQ sauce** | | |
| Ketchup | 250 g | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 2 tbsp (40 g) | |
| Honey (asal / miel) | 2 tbsp (40 g) | |

No onion powder? Leave it out; the cooked onion in the sauce covers it. No smoked paprika? All sweet paprika.

**Creamy red chicken variant** (from the buffalo sliders, made mild): make the sauce from 60 g tomato paste, 1 tbsp sweet paprika, 25 g butter, 1 tbsp vinegar and 200 ml chicken stock instead of the ketchup, honey, cider vinegar and water. After shredding, stir in 60 g fromage à tartiner. About the same numbers a cube, with less sugar; label it `CREAMY RED`.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Rub** the chicken all over with the spice mix and leave it while you make the sauce.
2. **Sauce, small pot on medium:** oil and onion with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Add the garlic for 1 min, then the ketchup, tomato paste, honey, vinegar, mustard and water. Bubble for **2 min**.
3. **Slow cooker:** chicken in, sauce over, turn the pieces so they're coated. Lid on, **HIGH 2½ h or LOW 4–5 h**. It's ready when a breast pulls apart easily with a fork (74 °C in the thickest part). If it resists, give it 30 min more.
4. **Lift the chicken out**, shred it with two forks, and stir it back into the sauce.
5. It should be saucy but not wet. If there's a pool of thin sauce, leave the lid off on HIGH for **20 min** (or pour the sauce into a pot and boil it down for 5–10 min) before stirring the chicken back in.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, medium:** oil and onions with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min** until soft. Add the beef, bay leaf, salt and pepper and stir for **5 min**, until the meat loses its raw colour and releases its juices.
2. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon and coriander and stir **3 min**. Pour in the water and scrape the bottom clean so nothing catches.
3. **Lid on, high pressure 25 min**, then a quick release.
4. Open, and add the carrots, potato and green beans. Lid on again, **high pressure 5 min**, quick release. Pot instead: simmer the beef for **1¼–1½ h** until tender, add the vegetables and simmer **15 min** more.
5. Lid off on sauté for **5–8 min** to reduce, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beans. Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaf, and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. Grind the whole spices to a powder (about 2½ tbsp).
2. **Pressure cooker:** mince (broken up), drained split peas, onions, garlic, ginger, bay, ground spices, salt and at least the pressure cooker’s stated minimum thin-liquid volume (use 400 ml if allowed by its manual). Stir well. **High pressure 20 min**, let pressure release completely naturally; keep the cooker no more than half full because split peas foam.
3. **Sauté on high, lid off, 15–20 min**, stirring and scraping often, until every bit of liquid has gone and the mix looks dry and crumbly and starts to catch. This is the step that stops them going mushy. (Easier in a wide pan on a big burner if your cooker's sauté is weak.) Take out the bay leaf.
4. Spread the mix on a tray to cool for **20–30 min**. Don't leave it longer than an hour at room temperature; chill it if you're slower.
5. **Food processor:** pulse the coriander and mint until fine, then add the cooled mix in two batches and process each **about 1 min**, until smooth and paste-like. Taste the cooked mixture for salt first, then mix in 1 egg; do not taste the mixture after adding egg.
6. **Oven 230 °C.** With oiled hands, shape **28 patties**, about 50 g and 6–7 cm across. Dip each in the beaten egg, let the extra drip off, and lay them on 2 oiled parchment-lined trays. Brush the tops lightly with oil.
7. Bake **12–15 min, turning at 7**, until golden on both sides. Everything inside is already cooked; you're setting the egg and browning them. Air fryer instead: 200 °C, **6 min, turn, 5 min**.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, high:** oil, then brown the beef pieces **3 min a side**. Lift out.
2. Onions in with a pinch of salt for **5 min**, then the garlic, tomato paste and all the dry spices for **1 min**, stirring so the paprika doesn't catch.
3. Add the stock, lemon juice, vinegar, honey and bay, scraping the bottom clean (a stuck base trips the burn warning). Beef back in and turn it in the sauce.
4. **Lid on, high pressure 45 min**, natural release 10 min. Slow cooker instead: after step 3 everything goes in, **low 8 h** or high 4–5 h.
5. Lift the beef out and shred it with two forks. Take out the bay leaves. If the juices are thin, **sauté, lid off, 5–8 min** to reduce by about a third.
6. Beef back into the juices and stir well so it soaks them up. Add the coriander and taste for salt and lemon.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. 3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. - Produce: use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium heat:** butter and oil, then the onion for **6–8 min**, until soft with no raw bite. Add the carrot, celery and garlic for **4 min**.
2. Turn up, add the **beef** with the salt and pepper, and break it up for **6–8 min**, until no pink is left.
3. Add the glass of water, the nutmeg and herbs, and simmer until the water has almost gone (**~5 min**). Add the grated tomatoes, tomato paste and sugar, then turn it down and simmer with the lid off for **30 min**, stirring now and then. It should be thick but still **a little looser than you'd serve it**: the dry sheets need that liquid to cook.
4. **Oven 200 °C.**
5. **Burner 2, béchamel:** melt the butter on medium-low, stir in the flour for **2 min**. Off the heat, whisk in the milk a splash at a time. Back on medium, whisking, **6–8 min** until it coats a spoon. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper, then stir in the gouda off the heat.
6. **Build it** in the oven dish: a thin layer of béchamel, a layer of sheets (break them to fit, no gaps), a third of the bolognese, a ladle of béchamel. Repeat twice more, then finish with sheets, the rest of the béchamel spread right to the edges (bare pasta edges go hard), and the mozzarella.
7. **Bake 45 min**: foil on for the first 25, then off. It's done when a knife slides through the sheets with no resistance and the top is golden.
8. **Rest 15 min**, then cut into 6.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Produce: if batata hlowa is unavailable, replace with equal-weight peeled potato; for a sweeter result use half potato and half carrot, cooked until tender.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir; unsweetened peanut butter can be made by processing roasted unsalted cacahuètes until smooth; weigh the paste needed.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, medium-high:** oil, then the beef for **6–8 min**, stirring, until browned in patches. Add the onions for **4 min**, then the garlic for 1 min.
2. Add the tomato and tomato paste and stir **3 min** until the raw smell goes. Add the bay leaves, salt, pepper and the **600 ml stock**, and scrape the bottom clean.
3. **Lid on, high pressure 25 min**, then a quick release.
4. Open, add the carrots and sweet potato. Lid on again, **high pressure 4 min**, quick release. Pot instead: beef simmered **1¼–1½ h** first, then the vegetables **15 min**.
5. **Lower to the lowest heat.** Stir the peanut butter and hot water to a smooth paste, stir it in, and simmer gently with the lid off for **8–10 min**, stirring so it doesn't stick, until thick and glossy with a little reddish oil on top. Fish out the bay leaves and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. name: Beef taco soup

portion: 1/10 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice or mash cubes; add a chicken cube if more protein is needed

videos.title: Video embedded on the source page

sections.title: Ingredients (10 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Red kidney beans, dry (haricots rouges) | 300 g | soaked overnight (or 3 × 400 g cans, drained) |
| Lean beef mince (viande hachée maigre) | 800 g | |
| Oil | 10 ml (2 tsp) | |
| Onions (basal) | 2 medium (~300 g) | chopped |
| Peppers (poivrons), any colour | 2 (~300 g) | 1 cm dice |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1½ tbsp | |
| Ground cumin (kammoun) | 1 tbsp | |
| Dried oregano | 2 tsp | |
| Garlic powder, onion powder | 1 tsp each | |
| Dried dill (aneth) and dried parsley | 1 tsp each | the "ranch" part |
| Black pepper (felfel k'hal) | ½ tsp | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 60 g (2 tbsp) | |
| Tomatoes (tmatem) | 5 medium (~800 g) | chopped (or 2 × 400 g cans) |
| Sweetcorn (maïs doux) | 1 can (~285 g drained) | drained |
| Beef or chicken stock cubes | 2 | |
| Water | ~2 L | |
| Salt | to taste | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method.
2. **8 L pot on medium-high,** meanwhile: oil and mince for **8 min**, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned with no pink left. Spoon off any pool of fat.
3. Add the onions and peppers for **6 min**, until soft.
4. Turn to low. Add the garlic and all the dried spices and herbs for **1 min**, stirring, then the tomato paste for **2 min**.
5. Add the tomatoes, beans, corn, stock cubes and **2 L water**. Bring to the boil, then lid ajar and simmer **20 min**, stirring now and then.
6. Taste for salt. It should be thick and chunky with enough broth to ladle.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Nutrition (calculated)
sections.content:
**Assembly check:** one labeled soup serving + one [rice serving](../../recipes/riz.md) ≈ **570 kcal, 30.7 g protein**. A labeled serving may span several cubes. For more protein, add 0.5 of a labeled [mustard-chicken serving](../chicken/chicken-mustard-cream.md): about 739 kcal and 51.0 g protein in total. This is a lighter meal; increase a compatible starch or protein share if wanted.

name: Beef, bean and cheese filling cubes
label: BEEF, BEAN AND CHEESE FILLING CUBES
portion: 1/6 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (6 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| Oil, filling | 10 g |
| Onions (basal) | 150 g |
| Garlic (thoum) | 10 g |
| Beef mince, lean, raw (viande hachée maigre) | 600 g |
| Red kidney beans, canned, drained | 240 g |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 40 g |
| Paprika, cumin, oregano, garlic powder | 12 g |
| Salt | 6 g |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 150 g |
| Canned tomatoes, chopped/peeled (tomate pelée) | 300 g |

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Nutrition (calculated)
sections.content:
**Assembly check:** one labeled serving of this dish + one [rice serving](../../recipes/riz.md) + one [chakchouka serving](../../recipes/chakchouka.md) ≈ **656 kcal, 37.0 g protein**. A labeled serving may span several cubes.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 220 °C.** Toss the potato cubes with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt, and spread them on 2 parchment-lined trays in **one layer, not touching**. Roast **30–35 min**, turning once at 20 min, until golden and crisp on the edges and soft inside.
2. **Burner 1, wide pan, medium-high** (while the potatoes roast): the **beef** with the onion, broken up, for **8 min**, until no pink is left and the onion is soft. Add the red pepper and garlic for **3 min**. Heat off; stir in the soy sauce, salt and pepper.
3. **Burner 2, pot, medium:** melt the butter, add the mushrooms and cook **5 min**, until browned and their liquid has gone. Add the green beans for **4 min** (a couple more if frozen).
4. Sprinkle over the flour and thyme and stir **1 min**. Pour in the stock, then the milk, slowly, stirring. Simmer **4–5 min**, stirring, until it's thick and the beans are just tender. Heat off; stir in the mustard and cheese until melted.
5. Tip the beef into the sauce and stir. It should be a thick, creamy mix, not runny.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices. Lightly crush the cooked potatoes with a little hot water so they hold together in a mold. Divide beef and potato components separately into the same number of meal shares; label which cubes belong to one complete serving.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, medium:** butter, oil, grated onion, beef, bay leaf, pepper, paprika and salt for **10 min**, stirring, until the onion is soft and the meat has lost its raw colour. No browning needed; this stew stays pale.
2. Add the carrots and **500 ml water**. **Lid on, high pressure 25 min**, then a quick release.
3. Open, add the peas and artichoke hearts, and simmer with the lid off on sauté for **15 min**, until the peas are tender but still green. (Pot instead: simmer the beef 1¼–1½ h first, then the vegetables 15 min.)
4. Stir the flour paste again and stir it in for **3 min** until the sauce turns silky and lightly thickened. Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Taste for salt and fish out the bay leaf.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

1. **Big pot, medium-high:** oil, then the beef in big lumps. Leave it **3 min** to brown, then break it up and cook **4–5 min** until no pink is left. Spoon off any excess fat.

3. Pour in the milk slowly, whisking all the time so no lumps form, then the **700 ml water** and stock cubes. Bring to a gentle simmer, whisking often, for **4–5 min**, until it coats the back of a spoon. Keep the heat moderate; milk catches easily.
4. Add a third of the broccoli (~500 g, the stalks and the biggest florets) and the beans. Simmer **6 min**, until the broccoli is soft. Blend until smooth, in batches in the blender (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender), and return it to the pot.
5. Add the rest of the florets and simmer **6–8 min**, stirring, until just tender. They soften more when reheated.
6. **Turn the burner off** and let it stop bubbling. Stir in the mustard, nutmeg, pepper, grated cheese and processed cheese until melted. Cheese stirred into boiling soup goes grainy and oily. Taste for salt; the cheese is salty already.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required.
