sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker:** lentils, water, tomato, garlic, ginger, ground coriander, cumin, paprika, turmeric and salt. Stir. **High pressure 18 min** (20 min if you didn't soak), then natural release 5 min and release the rest.

4. Pour the tarka, fat and all, into the dal. Simmer **3 min**. It should be thick but still loose enough to pour off a spoon; if it's too stiff, add a splash of boiling water, and if it's thin, simmer 5 min more.
5. Off the heat: garam masala, lemon juice and herbs. Taste for salt.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- Use the specified fine or coarse boulgour. For a cooked spoonable grain mixture, the same dry weight of frik is an alternative: simmer separately until tender and drain excess water before mixing, rather than just soaking it as for fine bulgur.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. **Burner 1, pan, medium:** smen and the chopped onion for **6 min**, until soft. Add the almonds for 1–2 min until just golden. Add the filling mince, break it up and cook **8 min**, then stir in half the spice mix, the raisins and 1 tsp of salt. Spoon off any fat. **Spread on a plate and cool for 20 min.**
2. **Crust, food processor:** blitz the quartered onion to a fine purée. Add the cold mince and the rest of the spice mix and process to a smooth paste. Add the squeezed bulgur a handful at a time, processing in short bursts, with a splash of ice water if it's stiff. It should be smooth, soft and a bit sticky. (Do it in 2 batches if your processor is small.)
3. **Oven 200 °C.** Oil a 30 × 22 cm dish generously. Wet your hands with ice water and press **half the crust** into the dish in an even layer about 1 cm thick.
4. Spread the **cooled** filling to the edges, then flatten the remaining crust in 2–3 patties on baking parchment, flip them over the filling and peel the paper off, joining the gaps with wet fingers. Smooth the top.
5. Score diamonds or 6 big squares with a knife (cut right through), and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
6. Bake **40–45 min**, until deep golden and 74 °C in the middle. Rest 10 min.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 230 °C** (fan 210 °C) with 2 parchment-lined trays inside for the last 5 min: a hot tray sears the bites instead of stewing them.
2. **Toss** the chicken with the oil, Cajun mix and salt in a big bowl until every piece is red all over.
3. **Spread the bites on the hot trays** in one layer with gaps between them. Roast **12–15 min** without stirring, then **2–3 min** under the grill (or on the top shelf) until the edges darken. Cut the biggest cube: white all the way through, with clear juices (74 °C).
4. **Tip them back into the bowl** with all the tray juices, the melted butter, lemon and parsley. Toss.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. name: Carrot and cheese custard cubes
label: CARROT AND CHEESE CUSTARD CUBES
portion: 1/8 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: compatible protein and starch cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (8 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| Carrots (zroudiya) | 1200 g |
| Onions (basal) | 300 g |
| Vegetable oil (huile de table) | 36 g |
| Ras el hanout, cumin, black pepper | 8 g |
| Salt | 12 g |
| Eggs (œufs), ~50 g each without shell | 300 g without shell (about 6 eggs) |
| Cooking cream ~20% (crème cuisson) | 400 ml |
| Mustard, Dijon (moutarde) | 30 g |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 160 g |

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.
2. Chop vegetables small. Use the listed fat to soften onion/leek for 8–10 min; add garlic for 1 min. Cook mushrooms until their liquid evaporates, spinach until wilted and drained, and grated carrot, pepper or squash until tender. Cook any raw chicken separately in the same pan to 74 °C. Cool the filling briefly.
3. Beat the eggs with the listed milk, cream or fromage blanc and seasoning; stir in any listed flour and breadcrumbs. Stir in the cooked filling, grated/crumbled cheese and ready-cooked tuna/cachir if listed. Distribute all solid ingredients evenly.
4. Fill oven-safe cavities no more than three-quarters full. Bake about 20–35 min, depending on cavity size, until the centre is set and reaches 74 °C. A shallow dish can take longer. Rest 5 min, then follow the cooling and cube packing steps; keep the cooked filling soft rather than browning it crisp.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 180 °C.** Lightly oil 15 holes of the silicone muffin trays.
2. In a big bowl, whisk the eggs, both sugars, yogurt, oil and vanilla sugar until smooth. Stir in the carrots.
3. In a second bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate, spices and salt.
4. Tip the dry into the wet and stir **only until no dry flour is left** (overmixing makes them dense). Fold in the raisins.
5. Fill the moulds almost to the top (~95 g each), sprinkle each with a pinch of brown sugar.
6. Bake **22–25 min**, until domed and golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool 5 min in the trays, then unmould onto a rack and **cool completely**.


**Cube version:** use the completed baked mixture, including any listed glaze, after it has set. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.

1. **Grate the carrots** with the food processor's fine grating disc, in batches.
2. **Pressure cooker on sauté** (or high heat): 50 g ghee, the cardamom and all the carrots. Stir for **8–10 min**, until they collapse and the colour deepens.
3. Pour in the **milk**, stir, and scrape the bottom clean so nothing is stuck (a stuck base trips the burn warning). **Lid on, high pressure 30 min**, natural release 5 min, then release the rest.
4. **Lid off, sauté on high** (or a wide pot on the biggest burner, which dries it faster): stir every couple of minutes for **15–20 min**, until almost all the liquid has gone and it starts to catch on the bottom.
5. Add the sugar, milk powder, raisins, almonds and the last 30 g ghee. Keep stirring and scraping for **10–12 min**, until it's dry, glossy and pulls away from the pot, the ghee starts to show at the edges and the colour turns deep orange-red. That last fry is where the flavour comes from, so don't skip it. Fish out the cardamom pods if you can find them.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Béchamel first, so it can cool:** melt the butter in a pot over medium heat, stir in the flour for **1 min**, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer **5 min**, whisking, until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and leave it to cool for 15 min.
2. **Cauliflower:** boil it in salted water with the vinegar for **5 min**, until just tender. Drain it in a colander for **10 min** (wet cauliflower is what makes a gratin watery).
3. **Potatoes:** boil the slices in salted water for **8 min**, until just tender, and drain.
4. **Oven 180 °C.** Butter a large roasting dish (about 30 × 40 cm, or two smaller ones). Lay the potato slices over the bottom, then the cauliflower on top.
5. Whisk the eggs and parsley into the cooled béchamel and pour it evenly over the veg. Scatter the cheese over.
6. Bake **25–30 min**, until the middle is set (a knife comes out with no runny sauce) and the top is golden. Finish with **3–4 min** under the grill for colour.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Coconut milk is an optional shopping dependency: for each **100 ml**, use **75 ml whole milk + 25 ml cooking cream** if unavailable. Stir this alternative in near the end and heat gently; the sauce will be lighter and lose its coconut flavour.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Lentilles corail dissolve into the sauce. If only brown/green adas are available, cook them separately until soft before adding, then blend or mash if a smooth texture is needed; the same dry weight will have a different cooking time.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch; for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drained soaked chickpeas, fresh water to 3 cm above, **no more than half full**. **High pressure 12 min**, natural release 15 min. They should be tender but whole, as they cook more in the slow cooker. Drain.
2. **Frying pan, medium:** oil, cumin seeds and bay leaves for **30 s** until they sizzle, then the onion with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min**, then the paprika, coriander, turmeric, curry powder and cinnamon for **30 s**, then the tomato paste for **1 min**.
3. **Slow cooker:** potatoes on the bottom (they take longest), then the onion base, chickpeas, lentils, cauliflower, blended tomatoes and the 150 ml stock. Stir, lid on, **high 3½–4 h**, until the potatoes are soft right through and the lentils have melted.
4. Stir in the coconut milk and peas, lid back on, **high 20 min** more.
5. Off the heat: fish out the bay leaves, add the garam masala, lemon juice, coriander and salt to taste. It should be thick; if it's watery, leave the lid off for the last 20 min next time and ladle a little less liquid into each cube this time.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

name: Chana masala
label: CHANA MASALA
portion: 1/7 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Dried chickpeas (hommos / pois chiches) | 520 g | soaked overnight, 12+ h, drained |
| Bicarbonate of soda (bicarbonate) | ¼ tsp | optional, for extra-soft chickpeas |
| Oil | 40 ml | |
| Cumin seeds (graines de kammoun) | 1 tsp | |
| Onions (basal) | 2 medium (~300 g) | finely chopped |
| Garlic (thoum) | 4 cloves (20 g) | crushed |
| Fresh ginger (skinjbir) | 20 g | grated |
| Ground coriander | 1 tbsp | |
| Cumin (kammoun), sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 2 tsp each | |
| Turmeric (kourkoum) | 1 tsp | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 40 g | |
| Tomatoes (tmatem) | 450 g (3 medium) | blended |
| Salt | ~2 tsp | |
| Garam masala (mild; see local-supply blend) | 1 tsp | |
| Lemon (citron) | ½ (~20 ml juice) | |
| Fresh coriander (kosbor) | small handful | chopped |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drained soaked chickpeas, the bicarbonate, fresh water to 3 cm above, **no more than half full**. **High pressure 15 min**, natural release 15 min. They should be soft enough to crush with a spoon. Drain, keeping **400 ml** of the cooking water.
2. **Heavy pot, medium-high:** oil and cumin seeds; when they sizzle (15 s), add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook **8–10 min**, stirring, until evenly golden brown. If they catch, splash in 1–2 tbsp water.
3. Add the garlic and ginger for **2 min**. Turn to low, add the ground coriander, cumin, paprika and turmeric and stir **1 min** so they roast without burning.
4. Add the tomato paste and blended tomatoes, turn back to medium-high and cook **8 min**, stirring, until thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
5. Add the chickpeas, salt and the 400 ml chickpea water. Bring to a boil, then lid on, medium-low, **25 min**, stirring now and then.
6. Lid off, heat up, and crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pot with the spoon. Cook **3 min** more until it's thick and glossy. Off the heat: garam masala, lemon juice and coriander. Taste for salt.

Slow cooker instead of steps 5–6 (the Freezer Meals 101 way): tip the masala, chickpeas and water into the slow cooker, **low 4–6 h**, then crush and finish as above.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

**Assembly check:** one labeled serving of this dish + one [rice serving](../../recipes/riz.md) + one [chakchouka serving](../../recipes/chakchouka.md) ≈ **672 kcal, 23.3 g protein**. name: Chapli-spiced beef sauce cubes
label: CHAPLI-SPICED BEEF SAUCE CUBES
portion: 1/7 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Beef mince (viande hachée) | 1 kg | drained and patted dry |
| Coriander seeds (graines de coriandre) | 4 tbsp | toasted, roughly crushed |
| Cumin seeds (kammoun) | 2 tbsp | toasted, roughly crushed |
| Fine cornmeal (farine de maïs) | 50 g | toasted (step 2); chickpea flour works too |
| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~200 g) | very finely chopped, squeezed dry |
| Tomato (tmatem) | 1 firm (~120 g) | seeds out, finely diced, drained |
| Fresh coriander (kosbor) | ⅓ bunch (~30 g) | finely chopped |
| Garlic (thoum) | 4 cloves (20 g) | crushed |
| Ginger (skinjbir) | a 4 cm piece (15 g) | grated |
| Eggs (œufs) | 2 | beaten |
| Lemon juice (citron) | 2 tbsp | or 2 tsp pomegranate molasses if you find it |
| Black pepper (felfel k'hal), sweet paprika | 1 tsp each | |
| Salt | 2 tsp | |
| Oil | 2½ tbsp | for the trays and brushing |


**Additional sauce for the cube version**

| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| Crushed tomatoes (tomates pelées) | 600 g |
| Halal stock cube | 1 (10 g), dissolved in 250 ml water |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- Farine/semoule de maïs means ground maize, not Maïzena starch. If unavailable, fine wheat semolina can make a different soft semolina version; use the same weight and adjust moisture to the stated consistency.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. **Burner 1, dry pan, medium-low:** toast the coriander and cumin seeds for **3–4 min**, shaking, until fragrant. Crush them roughly (a few pulses in a grinder, or a mortar): you want some crunch, not a fine powder.
2. **Same pan, medium:** toast the cornmeal for **4–5 min**, stirring, until it smells nutty and darkens a shade. Tip it out to cool.
3. **Big bowl:** everything except the oil. Knead hard for **3–4 min** until the mix turns stringy and sticks together. Fry a teaspoon in a dry pan for 1 min and taste for salt. Chill **20 min** if you have time; it shapes more easily cold.
4. **Oven 230 °C.** Oil 2–3 parchment-lined trays. With oiled hands, shape **14 balls** (~115 g each) and press each out on the tray to a rough 10 cm round, **no thicker than ¾ cm**. Ragged edges are fine; they go crisp. Brush the tops with oil.
5. Bake **8 min**, flip, then **4–5 min** more, then **2 min under the grill** for colour. They're done at 71 °C in the middle. Don't push them further: over-cooked chapli goes dry and crumbly. Air fryer instead: 200 °C, **5 min, flip, 3 min**, two or three at a time.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **7 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

name: Cheeseburger soup
label: CHEESEBURGER
portion: 1/10 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice or mash cubes; add a chicken cube if more protein is needed
photoTitle: Healthy Dill-icious Cheeseburger Soup {Instant Pot or Stove Top}

sections.title: Ingredients (10 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Turkey or chicken mince (haché de dinde / de poulet) | 1.2 kg | ask the volailler to mince it in front of you |
| Oil | 15 ml (1 tbsp) | |
| Onions (basal) | 2 medium (~300 g) | chopped |
| Celery (krafes) | 3 stalks (~300 g) | chopped |
| Carrots (zroudiya) | 2 (~200 g) | small dice |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Flour (farine) | 30 g (2 tbsp) | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 30 g (1 tbsp) | |
| Onion powder, sweet paprika | 1 tsp each | |
| Black pepper (felfel k'hal) | ½ tsp | |
| Beef stock cubes | 3 | |
| Water | ~2.2 L | |
| Potatoes (batata) | 5 medium (~800 g) | 1.5 cm dice |
| Dijon mustard (moutarde) | 40 g (2½ tbsp) | |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 200 g | grated |
| Gherkins (cornichons) | ~200 g | chopped, plus 2 tbsp of their juice |
| Fresh dill (aneth) | a few sprigs (~15 g) | chopped, optional |
| Salt | only if needed (gherkins and stock are salty) | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Produce: use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **8 L pot on medium-high:** oil and mince for **6–8 min**, breaking it up, until no pink is left.
2. Add the onions, celery and carrots for **6 min**, then the garlic for 1 min.
3. Sprinkle in the flour and stir **1 min**, then the tomato paste, onion powder, paprika and pepper for 1 min.
4. Add **2.2 L water** a little at a time at first, stirring so the flour doesn't lump, then the stock cubes, potatoes and mustard. Bring to the boil, then lid ajar and simmer **20 min**, until the potatoes are tender.
5. **Off the heat,** wait 2 min until it stops bubbling, then stir in the cheese **a handful at a time** until each lot melts. Boiling it now would make the cheese stringy and grainy.
6. Stir in the gherkins, their juice and the dill. Taste before adding any salt.

Pressure cooker instead (8 L or bigger, no more than two-thirds full): after step 4's liquid goes in, lid on, **4 min high pressure**, 10 min natural release, then carry on from step 5.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, pepper and garlic. Cut chicken into 1–2 cm pieces. Cook onion and pepper in the oil for 8 min, add garlic and mild spices for 1 min, then flour, cocoa and tomato paste for 1 min.
2. Whisk in tomato coulis and the stock cube dissolved in 250 ml water. Add chicken and simmer gently 12–18 min until the chicken reaches 74 °C.
3. Fold in cooked drained beans and simmer 5 min. Turn heat low, melt in the fromage rouge, then remove from the heat and stir in plain yogurt, lemon and coriander. Divide the moist filling into molds; use a separate rice cube instead of tortilla layers.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Chicken (burner 1):** toss the chicken with the spice mix. Big frying pan or pot, oil, high heat, half the chicken for **6–7 min**, turning, until browned and cooked through with no pink inside. Repeat with the rest.
2. **Pasta and broccoli (burner 2):** boil the penne in plenty of salted water, **2 min less than the packet**. Add the broccoli for the **last 2 min**, then drain the two together.
3. **Sauce (burner 3):** melt the butter on medium, add the garlic for **1 min** (don't let it brown), stir in the flour for **1 min**. Whisk in the milk a splash at a time, then simmer **3–4 min**, whisking, until it coats the back of a spoon. **Heat off:** stir in the cream, fromage rouge, half the gouda, the nutmeg and the spinach (it wilts in the heat). Taste for salt.
4. **Oven on at 200 °C.** In your largest oven dish, fold together the pasta and broccoli, the chicken and the sauce. It should be loose and saucy. Spread level and scatter the rest of the gouda over.
5. **Bake 20 min**, until bubbling and golden on top.

2. Add the onion to the cleared side for **5 min** until soft and golden, then the garlic and ginger for 1 min. Stir it all together.
3. Whisk the soy sauce, peanut butter, vinegar, water, pepper and onion powder in a jug until smooth.
4. Add the carrots and cabbage (in two lots if the pot is full; it wilts fast), pour over the soy mix and stir-fry for **6–8 min**, until the cabbage is soft but still has a little bite.
5. Stir in the frozen peas for **2 min**, until they're hot. Taste: it should be well seasoned (the freezer dulls it), so add a splash more soy if it's flat. Scatter over the sesame seeds.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C.** Slit the whole eggplants in several places, push a slice of garlic into each slit, wrap each in foil and roast on a tray for **40–45 min**, until completely soft. (Start this first; it's the long step.)
2. **Sauce, burner 1, medium,** meanwhile: oil and garlic for 30 s, then the tomatoes, paste, paprika, salt, pepper, thyme, basil and sugar. **Simmer 20–25 min**, lid half on, until reduced and thick. Take out the thyme sprig.
3. Let the eggplants cool for **10 min**, peel, squeeze out the juice and mash the flesh with a fork (about 450 g).
4. In a big bowl, mix the chicken mince, mashed eggplant, coriander, cumin, salt, pepper and the 50 g of crumbs with your hand until even. It will be soft; add a spoon more crumbs only if you can't roll it.
5. **Oven up to 210 °C.** Put the beaten egg and the 40 g of crumbs in two shallow bowls. Wet your hands, roll **42 balls** (about 2 tbsp, ~43 g each), then dip each in egg and roll in crumbs (a light coat is enough). Lay them on two parchment-lined, lightly oiled trays, not touching.
6. Bake **20–22 min**, turning once and swapping the trays at 10 min, until golden and 74 °C in the middle (cut one open: no pink).
7. Tip the meatballs into the sauce and turn gently; **simmer 3–4 min**. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.

2. **Quince, burner 2, medium:** put the sugar, 400 ml water, cinnamon and star anise in a wide pot and bring to the boil. Add the quince wedges (drop them in as you cut them, or they brown), the raisins and the lemon juice. **Lid half on, simmer 20–30 min**, turning them once, until a knife slides in easily but the wedges still hold their shape. 4. Lift the quince and raisins out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Fish out the cinnamon and star anise, then **boil the quince syrup hard for 5 min** until it's reduced to a few spoonfuls of thin syrup, and pour it into the chicken.
5. Lid off, **simmer the chicken 5 min** to thicken the sauce. Gently fold in the quince and raisins (don't stir hard or the wedges break) and the orange blossom water. Taste for salt and lemon.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Large pot, medium-high:** oil, then the mince in 2 batches, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, **6–7 min** a batch until no pink is left and it's lightly browned. Scoop it into a bowl.
2. **Same pot, medium:** onions and peppers with a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Turn the heat to low, add the garlic, chili mix and tomato paste and stir for **1–2 min** (paprika scorches and goes bitter on high heat).
3. Add the tomatoes, stock, beans, sweetcorn and the mince. Bring to a boil, then simmer with the lid half on for **30 min**, stirring every 10 min so the bottom doesn't catch. Slow cooker instead: after step 2, tip everything in and cook on HIGH for 3 h.
4. It's ready when a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail for a second. Taste for salt and pepper and stir in the coriander.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Big pot, medium-high:** 1 tsp oil and the sausage slices for **4–5 min** until browned on both sides. Lift out onto a plate.
2. Toss the chicken with half the Cajun mix. The rest of the oil, then the chicken for **5–6 min**, turning, until browned all over. It finishes cooking with the rice. Lift it out with the sausages. Browned bits on the bottom are good; they're flavour.
3. Medium heat. The onions, peppers and celery for **6–7 min** until soft, scraping the bottom as they release their water. Add the garlic, the rest of the spice mix and the bay leaves for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for **1 min**.

5. **Lid on, lowest heat, 18 min.** Don't lift the lid. Heat off and leave it covered **5 min**. The rice should be tender with the liquid absorbed; if it's still wet, give it 2–3 min uncovered.
6. Fish out the bay leaves, fold gently so the meat is spread through the rice, and stir in the parsley. Taste for salt.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Cut chicken into 1–2 cm pieces and cook in 20 g butter until it reaches 74 °C. Add chopped spinach, cook until wilted and let excess liquid evaporate.
2. In another saucepan melt the remaining 40 g butter, stir in 40 g flour for 1 min, then whisk in 550 ml milk. Simmer 4–5 min until smooth and thick.
3. Fold in the chicken, spinach, fromage blanc, tomato coulis, nutmeg, pepper and grated cheese. Heat gently until the cheese melts. Divide into molds with the solids shared evenly. The crêpes and egg filling binders are omitted; assemble with a starch cube.

3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Dust the chicken:** toss it in a bowl with 20 g of the flour until evenly coated.
2. **Heavy pot, medium:** butter and oil until sizzling. Brown the chicken in 2 batches, leaving it alone for **4–5 min a side** until golden and a brown crust has formed on the bottom of the pot. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Lift it out.
3. **Onion, celery, carrots and garlic** into the pot for **5 min**, using their moisture to scrape up the brown bits, until the onion is soft. Stir in the other 20 g of flour for **2 min**.
4. Return the chicken with the potatoes, herbs and stock, and stir to lift anything stuck. Bring to a boil with the lid on, then **lid off, medium-low, 30 min**, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are tender and the gravy coats a spoon. Pressure cooker instead: steps 2–3 on sauté, then **high pressure 10 min**, natural release, and simmer 5 min lid off if it's thin.
5. Check the biggest piece of chicken (74 °C, no pink), taste for salt and stir in the parsley.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinate (the night before, or at least 2 h).** In a big bowl mix the yogurt, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, lemon, garam masala, ground coriander, turmeric, cumin seeds, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp of the oil. Stir in the chicken, cover and chill.
2. **Rice:** rinse the basmati 3–4 times until the water runs almost clear, then soak it in cold water for **30 min**.
3. **Fried onions (burner 1, the heavy pot):** the rest of the oil and the onions on medium for **15–20 min**, stirring more often at the end, until **deep golden brown** (not black; they turn bitter). Lift out half onto a plate for layering.
4. **Chicken (same pot, onions still in):** tip in the chicken and all its marinade. Bring to a simmer, lid half on, and cook **20 min**, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick and clings, not soupy. Stir in the peas for the last **3 min**. Fish out the cinnamon, cloves and cardamom pods.
5. **Par-boil the rice (burner 2, big pan):** meanwhile bring 3 L of water to the boil with 1 tsp salt and the cumin and coriander seeds. Add the drained rice and boil **4 min** only; it should still be firm in the middle. Drain.
6. **Layer:** spread the chicken level in the pot. Scatter half the reserved onions, half the coriander and all the mint, then all the rice, then the rest of the onions and coriander. Drizzle the turmeric milk and melted butter over the top.
7. **Steam:** lay a sheet of foil over the pot and press the lid on tight. **Lowest heat, 20 min**, then heat off and leave it shut for **5 min**. The rice should be tender and fluffy all through; if the top is still firm, sprinkle 2 tbsp water over it and give it 5 min more.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

| Chicken stock cube | 1 | crumbled |
| Dijon mustard (moutarde) | 1½ tbsp (20 g) | |
| Cachir, turkey or chicken | 120 g | 1 cm dice |
| Emmental or gruyère (emmental râpé) | 80 g | grated |
| Nutmeg, black pepper | a pinch each | |
| **Crumb topping** | | |
| Breadcrumbs (chapelure) | 50 g | |
| Butter | 10 g | melted |
| Dried thyme or parsley | a pinch | |

Cheaper: *fromage rouge* instead of Emmental; the sauce is a bit milder.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Crumbs first:** oven 200 °C. Toss the breadcrumbs with the melted butter and herbs, spread them on a small tray and toast **6–8 min**, stirring halfway, until golden. Cool completely, then tip into a small zip bag (`CB CRUMBS`).
2. **Large pot, medium-high:** oil, then the chicken in 2 batches for **4–5 min** each, until golden outside. Lift it out.
3. **Medium heat:** butter and onion with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min**, until soft with no raw bite; garlic for 1 min. Stir in the flour for **1–2 min**.
4. **Pour the milk in slowly**, whisking so no lumps form, then add the stock cube. Simmer **3–4 min** until thick. Add the chicken and its juices and simmer gently for **8–10 min**, stirring often so the bottom doesn't catch, until the biggest cube is white all through (74 °C).
5. **Off the heat:** stir in the mustard, cachir, cheese, nutmeg and pepper until the cheese melts. Taste before salting; the cachir and stock are already salty.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

1. **Marinade:** in your biggest bowl, whisk the oil, lemon juice, orange juice, sugar, fajita mix, garlic, salt and pepper. Take out 2 tbsp into a second bowl for the vegetables. Toss the chicken strips in the big bowl and leave them in the fridge for **30 min** (up to 4 h).

3. **Spread everything in one layer**: chicken on 2 trays, vegetables on the third. Crowded trays steam instead of roasting. If only 2 trays fit in the oven, roast the vegetables first and keep them warm under a tea towel while the chicken goes in.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Rice (burner 2, first job of the session):** rinse it twice, then boil in plenty of salted water for **10–11 min** until just tender. Drain well and **spread it straight onto 2 trays** in a thin layer. Cool **15 min** on the counter, then into the fridge uncovered for **1 hour**. Cold, dry rice is what makes fried rice work; warm rice goes mushy. (Or cook it the evening before, chill it on trays the same way, and cover it once cold.)
2. **Chicken (burner 1, big pot or wok, high heat):** 1 tbsp oil, then half the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy. Stir-fry **5–6 min** until cooked through with no pink in the middle. Lift out into a bowl and repeat with the second half. Two batches keep it frying rather than stewing.
3. **Egg:** ½ tbsp oil, pour in the eggs and scramble **1–2 min** until just set. Tip onto the chicken.
4. **Veg:** the rest of the oil, then the onion, carrot and celery for **5 min** until the carrot is soft. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min**, then the peas for **2 min**.
5. **Rice:** add the cold rice, break up the clumps with the spoon, and fry **5 min**, turning it over and over, until it's hot and some grains start to toast.
6. Pour over the rest of the soy and the honey, add the pepper, then tip the chicken and egg back in. Toss **2–3 min** until everything is steaming hot. Taste; add a splash more soy if it's bland.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; choose firm pizza mozzarella; the same weight of grated fromage rouge works with less stretch.

- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.content:

2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, high:** smen and oil in your widest pan. Onion for **5–6 min** until lightly golden, then the garlic and ginger for **1 min**.
2. Add the chicken with ½ tsp salt and stir-fry for **5 min**, until it's white all over and stops releasing water.

4. **Heat to medium, lid on, 12 min**, stirring once. The tomatoes break down into a lot of juice.
5. **Lid off, heat to high, 10–15 min**, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the juice has cooked off into a thick, glossy masala and the oil separates at the edges. (Boneless thighs release more water than bone-in, so this step takes a bit longer; don't stop until it's thick.)
6. Heat to medium, add the whisked yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring, and cook gently for **2–3 min**. Stir in the black pepper and garam masala. Chicken should be white all the way through. **Off the heat**, scatter over the ginger matchsticks and coriander. Taste for salt.

5. **Tomato masala, burner 1, medium,** while they bake: oil and onion for **8 min** until soft and golden, garlic and ginger for 1 min, spices for 30 s, then the tomatoes, water, salt and sugar. **Simmer 12–15 min**, lid half on, until slightly thickened. Blend smooth if you like.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: if feta is unavailable, use the same weight of firm, well-drained plain jben, crumble it and season to taste; do not use dried klila as a direct substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- For each **50 g drained sun-dried tomatoes**, a local alternative is **100 g sweet red pepper + 15 g tomato concentrate**: dice and cook the pepper with the onion until soft, then fry the paste for 1 min. Reduce the extra moisture before freezing.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C**, two trays lined with parchment and lightly oiled.
2. In a big bowl, mix everything in the meatball list with your hand until just even. Don't overmix or they go tough. The mix is soft; wet hands help.
3. Roll **42 balls** of about 2 tbsp (~40 g; an ice-cream scoop makes them all the same size) and lay them on the trays, not touching.
4. Bake **18–20 min**, swapping the trays at 10 min, until golden and 74 °C in the middle (cut a big one open: no pink).
5. **Sauce, burner 1, medium,** while they bake: oil and onion for **6–8 min** until soft, garlic for 30 s, then the tomatoes, paste, herbs, sugar, salt and pepper. **Simmer 15–20 min**, lid half on, until thick.
6. Tip the baked meatballs into the sauce and turn gently; **simmer 3 min**. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté** (or a heavy pot on medium): oil and onions with a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Add the garlic for 1 min.
2. **Off the heat for a moment**, stir in the paprika and flour (paprika burns and turns bitter on high heat), then the tomato paste. Back on medium for **1 min**.
3. Add the chicken and peppers and stir to coat. Pour in the **400 ml stock**, scraping the bottom so nothing catches (a stuck base trips the pressure cooker's burn warning).
4. **Lid on, high pressure 8 min**, then natural release for 10 min. Pot instead: lid on, simmer **35 min**, stirring now and then.
5. **Off the heat**, let it stop bubbling (1–2 min), then stir in the crème fraîche. Boiling it now would split it. Add the parsley, and taste for salt and pepper.
6. It should be a thick, spoonable stew. If it's thin, simmer with the lid off for 5 min before the cream goes in next time; this time just ladle a little less liquid into each cube.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, medium-high:** oil in a heavy pot, then the onions. Fry for **12–15 min**, stirring, until golden brown. If they catch, splash in 2 tbsp water and scrape.
2. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min** until the raw smell has gone. Add the chicken with ¼ tsp salt and stir-fry for **2–3 min** only (boneless dries out if you fry it longer).
3. Add the whole spices, ground coriander, paprika, turmeric and the rest of the salt; stir for **1 min**, splashing in a little water if it sticks.
4. Add the tomatoes and red pepper and cook for **3 min**, until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
5. Pour in the **300 ml stock** (less water than for bone-in; the chicken and tomatoes release their own). Bring to a boil, then **lid on, low simmer 14–15 min**, stirring once, until the chicken is tender and white all the way through.
6. Lid off for the last **3–4 min** so the oil rises to the top and the gravy thickens slightly. **Off the heat**, stir in the garam masala and coriander. Taste for salt: it should be well seasoned.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium-high:** oil, then the mince. Break it up with a spoon and cook **10 min**, stirring now and then, until there's no pink left, the liquid has boiled off and it's starting to brown. Push it to one side (or lift it out if the pot is crowded).
2. Onion and mushrooms in with a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until the mushrooms have given up their water and gone golden. Garlic in for 1 min.
3. Stir in the flour, paprika and thyme for **1 min**, then whisk in the **hot stock** a little at a time with the Dijon. Simmer **5 min**, stirring, until thick and glossy, and everything is steaming hot.
4. **Off the heat**, let it stop bubbling (1–2 min), then stir in the crème fraîche, lemon juice, pepper and parsley. Taste for salt. It should be thick and spoonable; if it's thin, simmer 3 min more before the cream next time.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinate** (the evening before if you bought the chicken the day before, or first thing on cook day): mix everything in the marinade list in a big bowl or zip bag, cover and fridge for **4 h to overnight**. Not longer: the yogurt turns the chicken mushy.
2. **Oven 240 °C**, two trays lined with foil and lightly oiled. Spread the chicken out in one layer (shake off the excess marinade) and roast on the top shelves for **15–18 min**, swapping the trays at 8 min, until charred at the edges. It doesn't need to be fully cooked yet.
3. Meanwhile, **burner 1, medium:** butter and oil in a big heavy pot. Onion with a pinch of salt for **8 min** until soft and golden, then the cardamom, garlic and ginger for 1 min, then the ground spices for 30 s.
4. Stir in the tomato paste and cook **1 min** until it darkens. Add the tomatoes, squash and water. **Lid on, simmer 15 min**, until the squash is soft enough to crush with a spoon. Fish out the cardamom pods and blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender (or mash the squash hard against the side).
5. Tip in the charred chicken and any tray juices. **Simmer gently 10 min**, lid half on, stirring now and then, until a thick piece is white all the way through.
6. **Off the heat**, stir in the cream and the coriander. Taste for salt. It should be a thick sauce that coats the chicken; if it's thin, simmer uncovered for 3–4 min before the cream goes in next time.
