sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- Farine/semoule de maïs means ground maize, not Maïzena starch. If unavailable, fine wheat semolina can make a different soft semolina version; use the same weight and adjust moisture to the stated consistency.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method.
2. **8 L pot on medium,** meanwhile: oil, onions and peppers for **8 min** until soft.
3. Turn to low. Add the garlic and all the spices for **1 min**, stirring (paprika burns fast), then the tomato paste for **2 min**.
4. Add the blended tomatoes and cook **5 min**. Stir the cornmeal and water again and pour it in, stirring, then add the stock cubes and **1.3 L water**. Bring to the boil, stirring the bottom.
5. Slide in the **whole chicken breasts** and simmer gently, lid ajar, **18 min**. Lift the chicken out onto a board.
6. **For the smooth restaurant-style base (optional):** blend the pot now with a stick blender, before the beans and corn go in.
7. Add the beans and corn and simmer **10 min**, stirring now and then.
8. Shred the chicken with two forks and put it back. **Off the heat:** lemon juice and coriander. Taste for salt.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Coconut milk is an optional shopping dependency: for each **100 ml**, use **75 ml whole milk + 25 ml cooking cream** if unavailable. Stir this alternative in near the end and heat gently; the sauce will be lighter and lose its coconut flavour.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch; for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drained soaked chickpeas, fresh water to 3 cm above, **no more than half full**. **High pressure 15 min**, natural release 15 min, until they squash easily. Drain.
2. **Wide pot, medium:** oil and onions with a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger and coriander stalks for **1 min**, then the curry powder, cumin, ground coriander and turmeric for **1 min**, stirring (add a splash of water if they catch).
3. Add the tomatoes and cook **5 min**, until they collapse. Add the chickpeas, stock and coconut milk and simmer with the lid off for **10 min**.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; use plain fromage fondu portions, not a sweet or herb-and-garlic spread.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté** (or a big heavy pot on medium-high): oil, then the **beef** and onion, breaking the beef up, for **8 min** until no pink is left and the onion is soft. Add the garlic and the chili mix for **1 min**, stirring so it doesn't catch.
2. Heat off. Pour in the **750 ml stock** and **scrape the bottom clean**; anything stuck there trips the pressure cooker's burn warning.
3. Layer in, **without stirring**: the beans, the peppers, the macaroni (push it under the liquid), then the grated tomatoes, and finally the tomato paste dolloped on top. Tomato on the bottom burns, which is why it goes last.
4. **Lid on, high pressure 4 min** (count from when it comes up to pressure; it takes about 10). Then **release the steam in short bursts**, opening and closing the valve, so the starchy foam doesn't spurt. Never fill the pot more than half full with pasta in it; if yours is smaller than 8 L, use the pot method.
   **Pot instead:** after step 2, add everything, bring to the boil, then simmer with the lid half on for **10–12 min**, stirring every 2 min and scraping the bottom, until the macaroni is just tender. Add a splash of water if it gets thick.
5. Stir in the corn, plain processed cheese and gouda, lid back on (no pressure) for **5 min** to melt and settle. Taste for salt.
6. It should be **saucy and loose**; it tightens a lot as it cools. If it's already stiff, stir in 100 ml hot water.

Want it hotter? Harissa on your own bowl at the table, never in the pot.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Line a 20 × 20 cm dish** (or a 20 × 25 cm one) with baking paper, leaving an overhang so you can lift the slab out.
2. **Biscuit crumbs:** blitz the biscuits in the food processor until fine and even, like sand.
3. **Base:** put the butter and 260 g peanut butter in a microwave-safe bowl. **Microwave 30 s**, stir, then 15 s more if needed, just until they melt together. Don't get it piping hot.
4. Stir in the icing sugar and biscuit crumbs to a thick, even paste. Press it firmly and evenly into the dish with the back of a spoon.
5. **Top:** chocolate and the last 30 g peanut butter in a clean bowl. **Microwave 30 s**, stir, then **15 s bursts**, stirring each time, until just melted and smooth. Stop while a few lumps remain; stirring melts them.
6. Pour over the base, spread it smooth, and scatter the chopped peanuts over, pressing them in lightly.
7. **Fridge for 2 h** until completely set. Lift the slab out and cut into **15 bars** (3 × 5) with a sharp knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between cuts.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Produce: use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Kefta first:** mix the mince with the chopped parsley, ½ tsp salt, a pinch of pepper and a pinch of cinnamon. Roll about **40 marbles** (10 g each, a heaped teaspoon). Keep them covered in the fridge.
2. **8 L pot on medium:** oil and smen, then the beef cubes and grated onion. Cook **8–10 min**, stirring, until the meat has lost its red colour and the onion is soft.
3. Add the paprika, black pepper, half the coriander and the fresh mint for **1 min**, then the blended tomatoes and the cinnamon stick. Cook **3 min**.
4. Add the carrots, potatoes, celery, 2 tsp salt and **2.3 L boiling water**. Lid ajar, simmer **50–60 min**, until a beef cube breaks when you press it with a spoon.
5. Dilute the tomato paste in a ladle of the broth and stir it in. Add the zucchini, chickpeas and kefta (drop them in one by one so they hold together). Simmer **10 min**; cut one meatball open: no pink inside.
6. Shower in the vermicelli, stirring so it doesn't clump, and simmer **3–4 min only**. It should still have a little bite.
7. **Off the heat:** the rest of the coriander and the dried mint. Fish out the cinnamon stick and taste for salt.
8. Leave it brothy, a little thinner than you'd serve it: the vermicelli keeps drinking the liquid. You want about 5.2 L; top up with boiling water if you're short.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Oven 220 °C.** Peppers cut side down on a parchment-lined tray for **20–25 min**, until the skins blister and blacken in patches. Tip them into a bowl, cover with a plate for 10 min, then pull off the loose skin (don't fuss over every bit).
2. Meanwhile, **pressure cooker on sauté** (or a heavy pot on medium-high): half the oil, and brown half the beef for **4–5 min**, turning once. Lift it out, repeat with the rest. Browning in two lots matters; a crowded pot just stews the meat grey.
3. Lower to medium. Onions in the fat with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min**, scraping up the brown bits. Garlic for 1 min. **Off the heat**, stir in the paprikas, cumin, oregano, cinnamon and allspice (paprika burns fast), then the tomato paste; back on for 1 min.
4. **Blender:** peppers plus 300 ml of the stock, blitzed smooth. Pour into the pot with the rest of the stock and the beef, and scrape the bottom clean so the pressure cooker doesn't trip its burn warning.
5. **Lid on, high pressure 35 min**, natural release 10 min. Pot instead: lid ajar, the gentlest simmer for **2–2½ h**, stirring every 30 min, until a cube squashes easily against the side.
6. Back on sauté (or medium heat): stir in the cornmeal slurry and the vinegar and simmer **5 min**, stirring, until it thickens to a glossy sauce that coats the meat. Taste for salt and pepper.

1. **Big heavy pot, medium heat:** oil and onions with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and pale gold. Add the garlic for 1 min.
2. **Turn it up to medium-high**, add the mince and break it up hard with a spatula or a potato masher for **8–10 min**, until no pink is left and the liquid has mostly cooked off. Cincinnati chili is a fine, smooth meat sauce, so mash out every lump.

5. Stir in the beans and simmer with the lid off for **10 min**. It should be a thick, spoonable sauce; if it's still runny, give it 10 min more. Spoon off any fat pooled on top, fish out the bay leaf, and taste for salt.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Rub the beef with the salt, cumin, oregano, paprika and pepper.
2. **Pressure cooker on sauté, high:** oil, then brown the beef **3 min a side**. Add the onions and garlic for 2 min.
3. Pour in the orange juice, lemon juice, honey, bay leaves and the squeezed lemon half. Scrape the bottom clean. Keep the liquid to just this: less liquid means more flavour (the source's tip).
4. **Lid on, high pressure 60 min**, natural release 10 min. Slow cooker instead: after step 3 everything goes in, **low 8 h**.
5. Lift the beef out and shred it with two forks. Fish out the bay leaves and the lemon half. **Sauté, lid off, 8–10 min** to reduce the juices by about half.
6. **Oven grill (broiler) on high.** Spread the shredded beef on a parchment-lined tray, spoon over a ladle of the juices, and grill **5–8 min** until the edges brown and crisp. Watch it; it turns fast.
7. Tip the beef back into the pot with the rest of the juices and stir. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Lentils, small pot:** cover well with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer fast for **10–12 min**, until just tender but still with some bite. Drain.
2. **Onions, big deep frying pan or wide pot, low heat:** oil, butter, onions, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon. Fry very gently for **30 min**, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are meltingly soft and golden brown. Don't rush them on high heat; the slow browning is the flavour. Add the garlic for **1 min**.
3. Drain the rice and stir it into the onions to coat. Add the lentils, the **450 ml hot stock**, salt and pepper, and bring to the boil.
4. Lid on tightly (or a sheet of foil under the lid), lowest heat for **12 min**. Off the heat, still covered, rest **10 min**.
5. Fork it through to separate the grains, fishing out the cinnamon stick, and as many cloves and cardamom pods as you can find (biting one isn't nice). Taste for salt.
6. **Spread it on a tray straight away**, then while it's warm press it firmly into the silicone muffin trays, about 85 g per well, 20 wells.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Keep the drained canned tuna aside for the finish.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the drained tuna and olives and heat through. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drain the soaked chickpeas, cover with 5 cm of fresh water, **high pressure 20 min**, natural release. Drain. (Pot instead: simmer 1 h–1 h 15 min until creamy inside. Canned: just rinse them.)
2. **8 L pot, medium:** the oil, onions, celery and carrots with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin and turmeric for **1 min**, stirring so the spices don't burn.
3. Add the squash and stir to coat, then the lentils, stock cubes and **1.8 L water**. Bring to the boil, skim, then lid on and simmer **20–25 min**, until the squash is soft and the lentils have collapsed.
4. Blend until smooth, in batches in the blender (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender).
5. Back in the pot on low: stir in the coconut milk, chickpeas and spinach and simmer **5 min**, stirring so it doesn't catch. Off the heat, add the lemon juice, then salt and pepper to taste.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

3. Simmer the sauce with the already-cooked tender beans, lid ajar, for **15–20 min**. No further pressure step is needed.

sections.title: Ingredients (6 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount |

| Chicken breast, raw (escalope) | 750 g |
| Stock cube (bouillon) | 5 g |
| Spinach (sebnekh / épinards), fresh or frozen | 200 g |
| Processed cheese portions (Vache qui rit type) | 120 g |
| Gouda / fromage rouge | 100 g |

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; use plain fromage fondu portions, not a sweet or herb-and-garlic spread.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice the onion, garlic and vegetables; cut chicken into 1–2 cm pieces. Grate the cheese. Prepare only the ingredients in the table below.
2. In the listed butter/oil, soften onion for 8 min. Add garlic, chicken and mushrooms, where listed, and cook until chicken reaches 74 °C and mushroom liquid has evaporated. Add spinach or peppers, if listed, and cook until soft.
3. Stir in the flour, if listed, and cook 1 min. Dissolve any listed stock cube in 200 ml water, then whisk in that stock and any listed milk, a little at a time; if neither is listed, use 150 ml plain water. Simmer gently, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon; add a little water if too thick.
4. Turn heat low and stir in cream/cheese, mustard, lemon and herbs as listed. Heat gently until the cheese melts. Keep the sauce moist for molding and microwave reheating.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:

Sun-dried tomatoes are in jars at the bigger superettes. If you can't find them, use 2 tbsp more tomato paste and a diced red pepper (poivron rouge) with the onion.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- For each **50 g drained sun-dried tomatoes**, a local alternative is **100 g sweet red pepper + 15 g tomato concentrate**: dice and cook the pepper with the onion until soft, then fry the paste for 1 min. Reduce the extra moisture before freezing.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Big pot, medium-high:** oil, then the chicken with ½ tsp salt. Cook **6–7 min**, turning now and then, until browned in places. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet.
2. Medium heat. Add the onion for **5 min** until soft and see-through, then the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, paprika, oregano and pepper for **1 min**, stirring.
3. Pour in **1.1 L of the stock** (keep 200 ml back), scrape the bottom, and bring to the boil.
4. Stir in the **orzo**, turn to medium-low, lid off. Set a timer for **6 min**, **stirring every 1–2 min and scraping the bottom** so it doesn't catch.
5. Add the zucchini and cook **4–6 min more**, still stirring, until the orzo is **just tender with a little bite** (10–12 min in all). Add the reserved stock if it gets thick before the orzo is ready.
6. **Heat off.** Stir in the cream and fromage rouge until melted, then the basil. Taste for salt. It should look **too loose**, like a runny risotto; the orzo keeps drinking the sauce as it cools.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

name: Creamy chicken-sausage and tomato pasta
label: SAUSAGE PASTA
portion: 1/6 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: vegetable cubes; already contains its starch

sections.title: Ingredients (6 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken mince (haché de poulet) | 700 g | |
| Fennel seed (graines de fenouil / habbet hlawa), sweet paprika (paprika doux), dried oregano, garlic powder, black pepper | 1½ tsp lightly crushed, 1½ tsp, 1 tsp, ½ tsp, ½ tsp | mixed into the mince with 1 tsp salt |
| Chicken sausages, halal (saucisses de volaille) | 300 g | 1 cm slices |
| Oil | 1 tbsp (15 g) | |
| Onion (basal) | 1 medium (~150 g) | diced |
| Red pepper (poivron rouge) | 1 large (~200 g) | thin strips |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 30 g (1 heaped tbsp) | |
| Canned chopped tomatoes (tomate pelée concassée) | 2 × 400 g cans | with juice |
| Chicken stock cube | 1 | dissolved in 700 ml boiling water |
| Rigatoni or penne (pâtes) | 420 g | |
| Spinach, fresh or frozen (sebnekh / épinards) | 150 g | roughly chopped |
| Cooking cream (crème cuisson) | 200 ml | |

Can't find fennel seed? Use 1 tsp dried thyme and 1 tsp more paprika; it's less sausage-like but still good. Beef mince (viande hachée) works in place of the chicken mince, at about 150 DZD more a bowl.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Mix the chicken mince with the fennel, paprika, oregano, garlic powder, pepper and salt with your hands.
2. **Big pot, medium-high:** oil, then the seasoned mince in big lumps. Leave it **3 min** to brown, then break it up into bite-size pieces and cook **3–4 min more** until no pink is left. Add the sausage slices and brown **3 min**.
3. Medium heat. Add the onion and pepper for **5 min** until soft, then the garlic for **1 min** and the tomato paste for **1 min**.
4. Add the tomatoes and the **700 ml stock**, scrape the bottom, and bring to the boil.
5. Stir in the pasta, bring back to the boil, then a lively simmer with the lid off for **11–12 min**, **stirring every 2 min** so it doesn't stick, until **just al dente** (1–2 min under the packet). Add a splash of water if it gets thick before the pasta is ready.
6. Stir in the spinach for **1 min** until wilted, then **heat off** and stir in the cream. Taste for salt. It should look saucier than you'd serve it; the pasta drinks the sauce in the freezer.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:

2. Stir in the flour for **1 min**. Pour in the milk a little at a time, whisking out lumps, then simmer **3–4 min**, stirring, until it thickens.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté:** butter and onion with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Stir in the ranch mix for 30 s.
2. Pour in the stock and scrape the bottom clean. Lay the chicken in one layer.
3. **Lid on, high pressure 10 min**, then natural release for **10 min**. Check the thickest piece: white all through, 74 °C.
4. **Lift the chicken out** and shred it with two forks. Put the pot back on sauté, whisk in the fromage fondu and milk until smooth, and bubble for **2–3 min**. It should be like thick cream; if it's thin, give it 2–3 min more.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; if feta is unavailable, use the same weight of firm, well-drained plain jben, crumble it and season to taste; do not use dried klila as a direct substitute.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.
2. Chop vegetables small. Use the listed fat to soften onion/leek for 8–10 min; add garlic for 1 min. Cook mushrooms until their liquid evaporates, spinach until wilted and drained, and grated carrot, pepper or squash until tender. Cook any raw chicken separately in the same pan to 74 °C. Cool the filling briefly.
3. Beat the eggs with the listed milk, cream or fromage blanc and seasoning; stir in any listed flour and breadcrumbs. Stir in the cooked filling, grated/crumbled cheese and ready-cooked tuna/cachir if listed. Distribute all solid ingredients evenly.
4. Fill oven-safe cavities no more than three-quarters full. Bake about 20–35 min, depending on cavity size, until the centre is set and reaches 74 °C. A shallow dish can take longer. Rest 5 min, then follow the cooling and cube packing steps; keep the cooked filling soft rather than browning it crisp.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **18 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Prep the wings:** cut off the tips and split each wing at the joint into a drumette and a flat. Pat them **very dry** with paper towels (dry skin is what goes crisp). Split them into two bowls, about 1.8 kg each.
2. **Bowl A:** toss with the oil, lemon zest, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, pepper, oregano and salt. Keep the lemon juice aside.
3. **Bowl B:** mix the garlic, coriander, cumin, curry powder, oil, cider vinegar, 1 tsp soy and salt, and toss the wings in it until coated.
4. Cover both and **marinate in the fridge 1 h** (up to overnight, which suits cook weekend: do it the evening before).
5. **Oven to 220 °C.** Line 3 large baking trays with baking paper (a rack on top of each is even better). Lay the wings out in a **single layer**, skin side up, not touching, keeping the flavours on separate trays.
6. **Bake 40–45 min**, turning them and swapping the trays round at 25 min, until deep golden and crisp, the juices run clear, and the thickest drumette reads **74 °C** at the bone.
7. While they bake, make the **glaze**, small saucepan, medium heat: brown sugar, white vinegar, 2 tbsp soy and ketchup. Bring to a simmer, stir in the cornflour water and bubble **1–2 min**, until it coats a spoon.
8. When the wings are done, squeeze the lemon juice over the A wings. Tip the B wings into a bowl, toss them in the glaze, spread them back on their tray and **bake 5 min more**, until sticky.


**For cubes:** after cooking, remove all bones and cartilage, check carefully for fragments, and chop the edible meat and skin. Keep the cooked glaze and tray juices; loosen with a little hot water and coat the chicken. Pack each flavour into separate molds. The microwave version will be tender, with no crisp-skin claim.

name: Dill pickle soup with chicken (zupa ogórkowa)
label: PICKLE SOUP
portion: 1/10 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice or mash cubes; add a chicken cube if more protein is needed

sections.title: Ingredients (10 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |

| Chicken breast (escalope) | 1 kg | left whole |
| Butter (beurre) | 40 g | |
| Onion (basal) | 2 medium (~300 g) | chopped |
| Carrots (zroudiya) | 3 (~300 g) | grated or small dice |
| Potatoes (batata) | 1 kg | peeled, 1.5 cm dice |
| Chicken stock cubes | 3 | |
| Water | 1.5 L + 250 ml | the 250 ml cold, for the flour |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux), garlic powder, dried thyme | 1 tsp, ½ tsp, ½ tsp | |
| Cinnamon, nutmeg, black pepper | a pinch, a pinch, ½ tsp | |
| Flour (farine) | 60 g (4 tbsp) | |
| Gherkins (cornichons) | 1 large jar: ~350 g drained + ~300 ml brine | grated or finely diced; keep the brine |
| Dijon mustard (moutarde) | 1 tbsp (15 g) | |
| Plain unsweetened yogurt (yaourt nature) | 250 g | |
| Fresh dill (aneth / shebt) | 1 bunch (~40 g) | chopped |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot, medium:** the butter, onions and carrots with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft. Add the paprika, garlic powder, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg and pepper for 1 min.
2. Add the potatoes, stock cubes and **1.5 L water**. Bring to a simmer, slide in the whole chicken breasts, and simmer gently, lid on, **15–18 min**, until the chicken is white all the way through (74 °C in the thickest part) and the potatoes are tender. Lift the chicken onto a board and shred it with 2 forks.
3. Shake the flour with the **250 ml cold water** in a jar until smooth, then stir it into the simmering soup. Add half the gherkins and all the brine and mustard, and simmer **5 min**, stirring, until it thickens.
4. Ladle about half the soup into the blender and blend until smooth (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender), then stir it back in.
5. **Off the heat:** stir a ladle of hot soup into the yogurt in a bowl to warm it, then stir that into the pot (straight in, it can curdle). Add the chicken, the rest of the gherkins and the dill. Taste: salt, pepper, and more brine if you want it tangier.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:
**Assembly check:** one labeled soup serving + one [rice serving](../../recipes/riz.md) ≈ **548 kcal, 32.1 g protein**. A labeled serving may span several cubes. For more protein, add 0.5 of a labeled [mustard-chicken serving](../chicken/chicken-mustard-cream.md): about 717 kcal and 52.4 g protein in total. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinate:** in a big bowl, mix the onion, garlic, lemon zest and juice, parsley, coriander, paprika, cumin, ginger, turmeric, salt and pepper. Add the chicken and turn it to coat. **30 min to 2 h** in the fridge.
2. **Olives:** put them in a small pot of cold water, bring to the boil on **burner 2** and boil for **3 min**, then drain. This takes out the bitterness and some of the salt so the sauce doesn't end up too salty.
3. **Burner 1, medium-high:** olive oil and butter in a heavy cocotte. Lift the chicken out of the marinade (keep the marinade) and brown it in two batches, **3–4 min** each, until golden on all sides. Set aside.
4. Tip the leftover marinade into the pot and cook for **5–6 min**, scraping the bottom, until the onion is soft and translucent.
5. Return the chicken with the sun-dried tomatoes and the water. Bring to the boil, then **lid on, simmer 15 min**.
6. Add the olives and simmer **10 min more** with the lid half off, until the chicken is tender and white all the way through and the sauce has reduced to a thick coating. Taste for salt only now.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. In a big bowl, rub the skinned drumsticks with the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt. Leave while you make the sauce.
2. Blitz the onions, garlic and ginger to a coarse paste in the food processor.
3. **Burner 1, medium-low:** melt the butter in a heavy pan. Add the whole berbere mix and stir for **1 min** (paprika burns on high heat and turns bitter). Add the tomato paste for 1 min.
4. Add the onion paste and the rest of the salt. Cook for **10–12 min**, stirring often, until it's thick, darker and smells sweet rather than sharp. (In Ethiopia the onions are cooked for ages; the slow cooker finishes the job.)
5. **Slow cooker:** drumsticks in, the onion sauce and stock over the top, stirred so they're coated. **Low 5–6 h** (or high 3 h), until the meat falls away from the bone.
6. Lift the drumsticks onto a tray with tongs and let them cool for **10 min**. Meanwhile, pour the sauce into a wide pan and simmer it hard on **burner 1** for **8–10 min** to thicken.
7. Pull the meat off the bones in big chunks (use two forks, or gloves); throw away the bones and any cartilage. Stir the meat back into the thick sauce and bring it back to a bubble for 2 min. Taste for salt; add a squeeze of lemon if it needs lifting.
8. **Pressure cooker instead:** steps 3–4 on sauté in the pot, then drumsticks and stock in, **high pressure 15 min**, natural release 10 min, then steps 6–7.


**Prepare for cubes:** After cooking, remove every bone and piece of cartilage and chop or shred the meat to 1–2 cm. Mix it with the cooked sauce and juices before filling molds; no bones go into a cube. For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.
2. Chop vegetables small. Use the listed fat to soften onion/leek for 8–10 min; add garlic for 1 min. Cook mushrooms until their liquid evaporates, spinach until wilted and drained, and grated carrot, pepper or squash until tender. Cook any raw chicken separately in the same pan to 74 °C. Cool the filling briefly.
3. Beat the eggs with the listed milk, cream or fromage blanc and seasoning; stir in any listed flour and breadcrumbs. Stir in the cooked filling, grated/crumbled cheese and ready-cooked tuna/cachir if listed. Distribute all solid ingredients evenly.
4. Fill oven-safe cavities no more than three-quarters full. Bake about 20–35 min, depending on cavity size, until the centre is set and reaches 74 °C. A shallow dish can take longer. Rest 5 min, then follow the cooling and cube packing steps; keep the cooked filling soft rather than browning it crisp.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **15 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

name: Eggplant chakchouka (chakchouka d'aubergines)
label: EGGPL CHAK
portion: 1/20 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: protein cubes + rice, pasta, couscous or mash cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (20 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Eggplants (bedenjal) | ~7 medium (2 kg) | 2 cm cubes |
| Olive oil (zit zitoun) | 3 tbsp (45 g) for the trays + 1 tbsp (15 g) for the sauce | |
| Salt | 1½ tsp | |
| Garlic (thoum) | 4 cloves (20 g) | crushed |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux), cumin (kammoun) | 2 tsp, 1 tsp | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 30 g (1 heaped tbsp) | |
| Tomatoes (tmatem) | ~10 (1.5 kg) | blended or grated (or 4 cans of chopped tomatoes) |
| Black pepper, a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes are sour | ½ tsp | |
| Fresh basil (hbeq), or parsley | a small handful (~10 g) | chopped |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- The listed ingredients are ordinary souk/épicerie items. Buy by metric weight; packet sizes and the size of individual vegetables vary.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 220 °C.** Toss the eggplant with 45 g olive oil and ½ tsp salt and spread it in one layer on 2–3 parchment-lined trays. Roast **25 min**, stirring halfway, until soft and golden.
2. **Sauce, wide pot, low heat, meanwhile:** 15 g oil and the garlic for **1 min**, then the paprika and cumin for 30 s (paprika burns fast). Add the tomato paste for 1 min, then the tomatoes, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Turn up to medium and simmer uncovered for **20 min**, stirring now and then, until thick.
3. Tip in the roasted eggplant and simmer **10 min** more, stirring gently, until the sauce clings to the eggplant and no watery liquid is left. Stir in the basil and taste for salt. Cool **30 min**.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **20**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **125 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Wide pot, medium heat:** oil, then onion for **6–8 min** until translucent and soft with no raw bite. Add the garlic for **1 min**.
2. Stir in the flour for **1 min** to make a paste, then the paprika, cumin and oregano for **30 s**. Pour in **200 ml** of the water and scrape the bottom so nothing scorches.
3. Add the tomatoes, the stock cubes dissolved in the other 200 ml water, and the salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, **lid ajar, 20 min**.
4. Blend smooth with a stick blender, then taste: add the sugar if it's sharp, and adjust the salt.
5. Put the chicken in the sauce, **lid on, low simmer 25 min**, turning once, until cooked through (74 °C). Lift out the chicken, shred it with 2 forks and stir it back in.
6. Simmer lid off **5–10 min** until the sauce is thick enough to coat the chicken.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Ingredients (12 recipe servings)
sections.content:

Water used for poaching or loosening is specified in the method. Weigh drained canned foods and edible meat; season lightly and taste after cooking.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Dairy: choose firm pizza mozzarella; the same weight of grated fromage rouge works with less stretch; if feta is unavailable, use the same weight of firm, well-drained plain jben, crumble it and season to taste; do not use dried klila as a direct substitute.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan. Whisk in flour and cook gently for 1 min.
2. Gradually whisk in the milk, then simmer 4–5 min, stirring, until smooth and thick.
3. Turn the heat low and stir in grated mozzarella and crumbled feta a handful at a time until melted. Add pepper, taste before adding salt, then spoon the thick sauce into small molds. Use as a rich sauce component with cooked vegetable and starch cubes.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **12 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **60 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Buy fish by cleaned, boneless edible weight and check for small bones. Canned tuna weights are after draining; count cans from their poids net égoutté, not the total tin weight.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Seasoning alternatives: parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Burner 1, potatoes:** cover with cold water, 1 tsp salt, boil and simmer **15–20 min** until a knife slides in (or pressure cooker, **8 min**). Drain, steam dry in the hot pot 2 min, then mash with the butter, warm milk, cheese, salt, pepper and nutmeg, using a masher.
2. **Burner 2, wide pot, medium-low** (while the potatoes cook): butter and leek with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and sweet with no bite.
3. Stir in the flour for **1–2 min**. Off the heat, pour in the milk a splash at a time, stirring, then the mustard. Back on medium, stirring and scraping the bottom, **4–5 min** until thick and bubbling.
4. Add the peas and corn for **2 min**, then the **fish chunks**. Fold them in gently, turn the heat to low and cook **4–5 min**, stirring as little as possible, until every chunk is **white and opaque all the way through** (break the biggest one to check). It'll firm up more when you reheat it.
5. Heat off. Stir in the cheese, dill and lemon juice, gently, and taste for salt and pepper.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices. For assembly, keep the cooked filling and mash separate instead of layering a large pie. Divide each into the same number of shares and freeze each component in its own molds; both sets together make the calculated meal.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce; washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Wide pot, medium:** oil, onion, carrot and pepper **8 min** until soft. Add the garlic, mushrooms and zucchini **5 min**.
2. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, water, herbs, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then **lid ajar, low, 40 min**, stirring often.
3. Stir in the spinach for the last **5 min**. Blend with a stick blender if he prefers it smooth. Taste for salt.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **14**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice the onion, garlic and vegetables; cut chicken into 1–2 cm pieces. Grate the cheese. Prepare only the ingredients in the table below.
2. In the listed butter/oil, soften onion for 8 min. Add garlic, chicken and mushrooms, where listed, and cook until chicken reaches 74 °C and mushroom liquid has evaporated. Add spinach or peppers, if listed, and cook until soft.
3. Stir in the flour, if listed, and cook 1 min. Dissolve any listed stock cube in 200 ml water, then whisk in that stock and any listed milk, a little at a time; if neither is listed, use 150 ml plain water. Simmer gently, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon; add a little water if too thick.
4. Turn heat low and stir in cream/cheese, mustard, lemon and herbs as listed. Heat gently until the cheese melts. Keep the sauce moist for molding and microwave reheating.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Toss the beef with the flour, paprika, pepper and a pinch of salt.
2. **Pressure cooker on sauté, high:** oil, then brown the beef in 2–3 batches, **3–4 min** a batch, until well coloured. Lift out.
3. Onions and mushrooms in for **5 min**, scraping up the brown bits. Pour in the stock and soy, scrape the bottom clean, then the beef and thyme back in.
4. **Lid on, high pressure 25 min**, natural release 10 min. A cube should cut with a spoon. Slow cooker instead: after step 3 everything goes in, **low 6–7 h**.
5. If the gravy is thin, **sauté mode, lid off, 5 min** to reduce it.
6. **Garlic butter, burner 1, small pan, low:** melt the butter and cook the garlic gently for **2–3 min**, until soft and just golden (not brown, or it turns bitter). Stir it into the pot with the parsley. Taste for salt and pepper.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Prep (~20 min).** Boil the kettle and make the 1.4 L of stock. Toss the chicken cubes with the salt, pepper and oregano. Wash the board and knife before you touch the veg.
2. **Big pot, medium heat:** oil, onions and a pinch of salt for **10 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Add the peppers for **5 min**.
3. Add the garlic, paprika, ground cinnamon and ½ tsp pepper and stir **1 min**. Keep it on medium; paprika burns fast. Add the tomato paste and stir **2 min**.
4. Add the chicken and stir **5 min**, until white all over.
5. Add the grated tomatoes, cinnamon stick, bay leaves and **800 ml of the stock**. Bring to the boil, then simmer with the lid half on for **10 min**.
6. Add the **orzo**, the zucchini and **400 ml more stock**; keep the last 200 ml back. Bring back to the boil, then turn to medium-low with the lid off. Set a timer for **10 min** and **stir every 1–2 min, scraping the bottom**, because orzo sticks. If it goes thick before the orzo is done, add some of the reserved stock.
7. At **10–12 min**, bite an orzo. Take the pot off the heat when it's **just tender with a little bite**; it softens more in the freezer and when you reheat it. It should look **too saucy**, like a loose risotto. That's right: the orzo keeps drinking the sauce as it cools.
8. Heat off. Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaves, stir in the parsley and lemon juice, and taste for salt.
