- Dairy: if feta is unavailable, use the same weight of firm, well-drained plain jben, crumble it and season to taste; do not use dried klila as a direct substitute.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- Lentilles corail dissolve into the sauce. If only brown/green adas are available, cook them separately until soft before adding, then blend or mash if a smooth texture is needed; the same dry weight will have a different cooking time.
- Ask for orge perlé, hulled/pearled barley. Dchicha is cracked barley: it is a possible same-dry-weight variant, but thickens and cooks faster; follow its texture and add water gradually.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté (high):** the oil, smen and onions for **8–10 min**, until lightly golden. Add the garlic, ginger and whole spices for 2 min, with a splash of water if it catches.
2. Add the beef and stir **5 min**, until it changes colour. Add the ground coriander, cumin, paprika, pepper, nutmeg, nigella and salt for 30 s, then the tomatoes, yogurt and **1.2 L water**. Scrape the bottom clean.
3. **Lid on, high pressure 45 min**, then natural release 10 min. The beef should break apart when pressed with a spoon; if not, 10 min more. (Pot instead: simmer covered 2–2 h 30 min.)
4. **Meanwhile, 8 L pot, medium:** the drained pulses, turmeric and **1.8 L water**. Bring to the boil, skim, then lid half on and simmer **45–50 min**, stirring every 10 min, until everything is soft and mushy (the split peas take longest). Add a little water if it gets too thick to stir.
5. Blend the pulses until smooth, with a stick blender in the pot or in the blender in batches (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender), and put them back in the 8 L pot.
6. Lift the beef out of the pressure cooker, fishing out the bay leaves, cinnamon stick and cardamom pods as you go. **Shred it** in a bowl with a potato masher or 2 forks into long strands. Tip the beef and all the cooking liquid into the pulses.
7. **Cook it down:** add the oats, and on low heat stir and mash against the side of the pot for **25–30 min**. It thickens and turns stringy and glossy (the "laced" look). **Stir often and scrape the bottom; it catches easily.** If it gets thicker than a thick porridge, add boiling water, 250 ml at a time. Stir in the garam masala and coriander and taste for salt.
8. **Leave it a little looser than you'd serve it:** it sets much thicker in the freezer.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |

| Chicken thighs, boneless skinless (cuisses de poulet désossées) | 1.25 kg | 3 cm pieces |
| Oil (huile de table) | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | |
| Onion (basal) | 1 large (~200 g) | 2 cm pieces |
| Garlic (thoum) | 3 cloves (15 g) | crushed |
| Fresh ginger (skinjbir) | 15 g | grated |

| Green pepper (felfel hlou) | 1 medium (~150 g) | 2.5 cm pieces |
| Carrots (zroudiya) | 2 (~200 g) | 1 cm slices |
| Soy sauce (sauce soja) | 5 tbsp (70 ml) | |
| Honey (asal / miel) | 3 tbsp (~65 g) | |
| Ketchup | 3 tbsp (~50 g) | |
| Smoked paprika (paprika fumé) | 1 tsp | |
| Canned pineapple chunks in juice (ananas) | 1 × 435 g can | drained, juice kept |
| Cornflour (maïzena) | 2 tbsp (20 g) | mixed with 4 tbsp of the pineapple juice |
| Toasted sesame seeds (jeljlane) | 1 tbsp (10 g) | optional |
| Black pepper | ½ tsp | |

Water chestnuts are optional and hard to find here; leave them out.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté:** oil and onion for **5 min** until soft, then the garlic and ginger for 1 min.
2. Add the chicken, carrots, soy, honey, ketchup, paprika, pepper and **100 ml of the pineapple juice**. Stir and scrape the bottom so nothing sticks (a stuck base trips the burn warning).
3. **Lid on, high pressure 5 min**, natural release 10 min, then release the rest. **Pot instead:** lid on, simmer 25 min.
4. Back on sauté. Add the peppers and **simmer 4 min**. Stir the cornflour slurry in and simmer **2–3 min** until glossy. Chicken must be 74 °C in the thickest piece.
5. Stir in the pineapple chunks and sesame, off the heat. Taste: a splash more soy if too sweet.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Cut the chicken into 1–2 cm pieces. Brown it in the oil in a wide pan in batches.
2. Reduce the heat, add butter and garlic and cook for 1 min. Stir in mild spices, honey, vinegar and 200 ml water.
3. Simmer gently 8–12 min until the chicken reaches 74 °C. Mix cornflour with 30 ml cold water, stir into the simmering sauce and cook 2 min, until it coats the chicken. Keep enough glaze to bind the pieces in molds.

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. sections.content:
1. **Oven 220 °C.** Line 3 trays with parchment.
2. Toss the carrots with the oil, thyme, coriander, salt and pepper, and spread them in **one layer** over the 3 trays.

5. Scatter the dill over and let them cool on the trays.

sections.content:
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- Épicerie alternatives: tahina can be made by finely grinding lightly toasted hulled jeljlane; thin with a little of the recipe’s oil and weigh the paste needed.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.

1. **Chickpeas:** drain the soaked chickpeas and put them in the pressure cooker with the bicarbonate and water to cover by 5 cm. **High pressure 25 min**, natural release 10 min. They should crush to a paste between your fingers; if not, 5 min more. Scoop out **200 ml of the cooking water**, put it in the fridge to go cold, and drain the rest.
2. **Garlic:** small pan, low heat: olive oil and sliced garlic for **2–3 min**, until soft and just turning pale gold, not brown. Take off the heat.
3. **Blend** the tahini, lemon juice, cumin, salt and 100 ml of the cold cooking water for **1 min**, until pale and fluffy.
4. Add the warm chickpeas, the garlic and all its oil, and blend **3–5 min**, scraping down twice, until very smooth. Add more cold cooking water a spoon at a time if it's stiff. It should be a little softer than you want to eat it; it firms up as it cools.
5. Taste: more salt or lemon if it needs it.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Finely chop the onion and garlic. Mix the meatball onion, 5 g garlic, beef, egg, breadcrumbs, parsley and half the seasoning. Form small 2 cm meatballs with wet hands.
2. Soften the sauce onion in olive oil for 8 min. Add the remaining garlic for 1 min, then tomato paste for 1 min. Add the tomatoes, sugar, remaining herbs and 150 ml water; simmer 10 min.
3. Add the meatballs and simmer gently 15–20 min until they reach 71 °C in the centre. Stir in mozzarella until melted, then portion meatballs and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C**, two trays lined with parchment.
2. **Meatballs:** in a big bowl, mix the soaked crumbs, eggs, cheese, fennel, garlic and onion powder, herbs, salt and pepper, then add the mince and mix with your hands just until even (over-mixing makes them tough). Rest 5 min, then roll about **35 balls** of a heaped tablespoon each (~33 g) with wet hands, 2 cm apart on the trays.
3. **Bake 15 min**, until browned. They don't need to be cooked through yet; they finish in the sauce.
4. **Sauce, while they bake:** wide pot on medium. Oil and onion for **8 min** until soft; garlic for 1 min; tomato paste for **2–3 min** until it darkens. Add the tomatoes, pepper, rosemary, sugar and salt. Simmer with the lid ajar for **20 min**.
5. Slide the meatballs and any juices into the sauce. Simmer gently for **10 min**, turning them once, until cut-open meatballs show no pink (71 °C in the middle). Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, wide pot, high heat:** oil, then the cumin seeds and onion. Stir for **8 min** until golden brown, not just soft. Add the garlic and ginger for **1 min**.
2. Add the mince in 2 lots, breaking it into small pieces with a wooden spoon, and cook **8–10 min** until no pink is left and most of the moisture has gone.
3. Add the tomato, yogurt, ground coriander, turmeric, paprika and salt, and cook **2–3 min** until the tomato starts to break down. Pour in **300 ml water** and bring to a simmer.
4. **Medium heat, lid on, 15 min**, stirring once. If the meat sticks to the bottom, add a splash more water.
5. Uncover, stir in the peas (canned and drained, or frozen straight from the bag) and cook **4–5 min** until they're hot. Add the black pepper and garam masala and stir for 1–2 min until the oil starts to separate from the sauce.
6. Off the heat, stir in the fresh coriander and lemon juice. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

Do not assume grams equal millilitres.

Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.

At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. **Oven 220 °C** (fan 200 °C), two trays lined with parchment and brushed with half the oil.
2. Mix everything except the oil in a big bowl and knead with your hands for **2 min** until sticky; kefta holds together because of the kneading, not an egg.
3. Divide into **28** pieces (~48 g). With wet hands, press each one into a finger about 12 cm long around a skewer, or just shape fingers with no skewer. Lay them on the trays and brush with the rest of the oil.
4. **Bake 12–15 min**, turning them at 7 min, until browned and cooked through: firm, no pink inside, juices clear (71 °C). A grill pan on cook weekend works too, 3–4 min a side.
5. Slide them off the skewers while they're warm.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, high:** oil, then brown the beef in two batches, **3–4 min** a batch, and lift it out. Browning adds a lot of flavour here; don't skip it.

4. **Lid on, high pressure 40 min**, natural release 15 min. Slow cooker instead: everything in after step 3, **low 6 h** (the source's tip: the full 6 h makes it more tender).
5. Lift the beef out onto a board and shred it with two forks. It should fall apart; if it fights you, give it 10 min more under pressure.
6. **Sauté on, lid off:** stir the cornflour mix into the sauce and bubble **2 min** until glossy. Beef back in, stir well, and add the sesame seeds. Taste; it shouldn't need salt.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; choose firm pizza mozzarella; the same weight of grated fromage rouge works with less stretch; buy unsweetened fromage blanc/jben frais; check the protein label rather than treating a sweet dairy dessert as equivalent.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot, medium-high:** the oil and mince for **8–10 min**, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left. Add the onions and carrot for **6–8 min**, until soft. Add the garlic, oregano, basil, fennel seed and nutmeg for 1 min.
2. Stir in the tomato paste for **2 min**, then the tomatoes, bay leaves, stock cubes, pepper and **1.5 L water**. Bring to the boil, then lid half on and simmer on low for **25 min**, stirring now and then. Taste for salt. Remove the bay leaves.
3. **Meanwhile, second burner:** a big pot of salted water at a rolling boil. Cook the lasagna pieces for **2 min less than the packet says** (about 7 min), stirring early so they don't stick together. Drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with a few drops of oil.
4. **Cheese cap:** in a bowl, mix the jben, mozzarella, fromage rouge, parsley and a grind of pepper.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. name: Lemon yogurt cake cubes
label: LEMON YOGURT CAKE CUBES
portion: 1/15 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: compatible dessert cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (15 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Butter (beurre) | 150 g | soft, plus a little for the tray |
| Sugar (sucre) | 200 g | |
| Eggs (œufs) | 4 | room temperature, beaten |
| Plain unsweetened yogurt (yaourt nature nature) | 250 g | |
| Lemons (qares / citron) | 3 | zest all 3, juice them (~120 ml) |
| Flour (farine) | 280 g | |
| Baking powder (levure chimique) | 1 sachet (~10 g) | |
| Salt | ¼ tsp | |
| **Glaze:** icing sugar (sucre glace) | 100 g | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Dairy: yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven to 180 °C.** Butter a 20 × 30 cm tray and line the base with baking paper, with an overhang on the long sides.
2. Zest the lemons, then juice them. Set aside **2 tbsp juice** and a pinch of zest for the glaze.
3. Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
4. In a large bowl, beat the soft butter and sugar with a whisk or electric mixer for **3 min**, until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs a little at a time, then the yogurt, the rest of the lemon juice and the zest. It may look curdled; the flour brings it back.
5. Fold in the flour mix in three goes, just until no dry flour shows.
6. Spread it evenly in the tray and **bake 30–35 min**, until golden, springy when pressed in the middle, and a knife in the centre comes out clean.
7. Cool in the tray **10 min**, lift out on its paper and cool completely on a rack (about 45 min).
8. **Glaze:** stir the icing sugar with the 2 tbsp lemon juice and the pinch of zest to a thick, pourable glaze. Spread it over the cold cake and leave **20 min** to set. Cut into **15 squares** (3 × 5).


**Cube version:** use the completed baked mixture, including any listed glaze, after it has set. Cut into pieces smaller than a mold cavity and press gently into 60 ml freezer molds; use the listed moist fruit/filling to bind crumbs, not raw batter. Pack separate flavours separately. A cake cube is a dessert component; serve it warm with a separately frozen fruit or yogurt component.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **15 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **60 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves; use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot on medium-high:** 1 tbsp oil and the beef in two batches, **5 min** each, until browned on all sides. Lift out each batch.
2. Turn to medium. The rest of the oil and the onions for **6 min**, scraping up the brown bits, until soft.
3. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, oregano and pepper for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for 1 min and the blended tomatoes for **3 min**.
4. Put the beef back with the bay leaves, stock cubes and **2.3 L water**. Lid on, simmer gently **45 min**.
5. Add the lentils, carrots, celery and potatoes. Simmer, lid ajar, **35–40 min**, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the beef is tender when pressed with a spoon. Green lentils can need 10 min more.
6. **Blend a quarter of it:** ladle about 1.2 L (no beef or bay) into a blender, blend smooth (lid vented, towel on top) and stir it back in. It makes the soup creamy.
7. Stir in the spinach for **3 min** until wilted. Off the heat, add the lemon juice and parsley, fish out the bay leaves, and taste for salt.
8. Leave it a little looser than you'd serve it: lentils keep thickening in the freezer.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.content:
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; buy unsweetened fromage blanc/jben frais; check the protein label rather than treating a sweet dairy dessert as equivalent.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Burner 1, wide heavy pot, medium-high:** 1 tbsp of the oil and **half the mushrooms**, in a single layer, **4 min** without stirring much, until browned. Tip them into a bowl and do the rest the same way. Crowded mushrooms steam instead of browning, and the browning is where the flavour comes from.
2. Turn to medium. The rest of the oil, the onion, carrots and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until the onion is soft with no raw bite. Add the garlic for 1 min, then the tomato paste for **2 min**, until it darkens and starts to catch on the bottom.
3. Add the mushrooms back, then the **lentils, bay, thyme, paprika, soy sauce and 1.4 L stock**, scraping the bottom. Bring to the boil, then lid on, low simmer for **25–30 min**, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and most of the liquid is absorbed. Take the lid off for the last 5 min if it's still soupy. It should be thick and spoonable; fish out the bay and taste for salt.
4. **Burner 2, potatoes** (start them when the lentils go in): cover with cold water, 1 tsp salt, boil and simmer **15–20 min** until a knife slides in (or pressure cooker, **8 min**). Drain, steam dry in the hot pot 2 min, then mash with the butter, warm milk and nutmeg using a masher. Beat in the **fromage blanc** last, off the heat. Season.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices. For assembly, keep the cooked filling and mash separate instead of layering a large pie. Divide each into the same number of shares and freeze each component in its own molds; both sets together make the calculated meal.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- If lait concentré non sucré is unavailable, gently reduce **2 ml whole milk to 1 ml** needed, then measure the reduced amount before use. Sweetened condensed milk is unsuitable for this savoury dish.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, medium-high:** oil in a big deep pan. Onion and peppers with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and the onion is golden with no raw bite. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 min.
2. **Heat down to medium-low**, stir in the curry powder, turmeric and flour and cook for **1 min**, stirring, so the spices toast without burning and the flour loses its raw taste.
3. Pour in the stock a little at a time, stirring out any lumps, then the mango nectar. Bring to a simmer: it thickens in a minute or two.
4. Add the chicken and stir so every piece is under the sauce. **Lid on, gentle simmer 12–14 min**, stirring twice, until a thick piece cut open is white all the way through.
5. Stir in the evaporated milk and jam and simmer **2 min more** with the lid off (evaporated milk won't split, so a gentle bubble is fine). Taste for salt and pepper; add the coriander.
6. It should be a thick, creamy sauce that coats a spoon. If it's thin, simmer uncovered for another 3–4 min.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze

1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- For each **50 g drained sun-dried tomatoes**, a local alternative is **100 g sweet red pepper + 15 g tomato concentrate**: dice and cook the pepper with the onion until soft, then fry the paste for 1 min. Reduce the extra moisture before freezing.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Season the chicken strips with the salt and pepper. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium-high:** oil, then sear the strips in two batches, **2–3 min a side**, until golden. They don't need to be cooked through yet. Lift them out.
2. Heat down to medium. Garlic and sun-dried tomatoes in for **1–2 min** until the garlic smells sweet and is just turning golden. Stir in the flour, thyme and basil for 1 min.
3. Whisk in the **hot stock** a little at a time, scraping the bottom, then the lemon juice and Dijon. Simmer **3 min** until it thickens.
4. Stir in the cream, bring back to a gentle simmer, and return the chicken with its juices. **Simmer 6–8 min**, stirring, until the chicken is 74 °C in the thickest strip. Don't boil hard or the cream can split.
5. Stir in the spinach for **2 min** until wilted (frozen spinach: 4 min), then the fromage rouge, off the heat. Taste for salt. It should be a thick, spoonable sauce; if it's thin, simmer 3 min more before the fromage rouge next time, and this time ladle a little less sauce into each cube.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Pot 1, high:** lentils, 1 L water and the stock cube. Bring to a boil, skim off the white foam, then **medium-low with the lid ajar for 20–25 min**, stirring now and then, until the lentils have no bite and mash easily. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick to stir.
2. **Pot 2 (wide), medium-high,** meanwhile: oil and cumin seeds for 15 s until they sizzle, then the onions and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for **30 s**, then the tomatoes, ground spices and salt. Cook **5 min**, until soft and the oil shows at the edges.
3. Add the spinach to pot 2 and cook **5 min** (frozen: 8 min), until wilted and the water has cooked off.
4. Tip the cooked lentils into pot 2 and simmer together **5 min**, stirring. It should be thick like porridge, thicker than you'd serve it, because each cube gets a splash of water at reheat.
5. **Tarka,** small frying pan on medium: smen, cumin seeds and sliced garlic for **1–2 min**, until the garlic is golden at the edges. Off the heat, stir in the paprika (it blooms in the hot fat), then pour it all over the dal and stir in. Add the garam masala, lemon juice and coriander, and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Paneer, the evening before (big pot, medium-high):** heat the milk gently to 85–90 °C, stirring so it does not catch. Off the heat, pour in the vinegar-water a little at a time, stirring gently, until the curds separate and the whey turns clear and yellow-green (you may not need all of it). Rest **5 min**.
2. Line a colander with a clean thin cloth (a new tea towel or *étamine*) and pour the curds in. Rinse with cold water to wash off the vinegar taste, gather the cloth and squeeze out the whey. Flatten into a 2 cm slab, still in the cloth, put a board and a heavy pot of water on top, and press **1 h in the fridge**, using a clean weighted container. Aim for **480 g of drained paneer**, but weigh the yield: milk type changes it. If short, make another small batch or recalculate for the amount actually used. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
3. **Masala, wide pot, medium-high:** oil and onions for **10–12 min**, until golden brown. Deglaze with 3 tbsp water, let it dry up and cook **2 min** more, until deeper brown. Add the garlic and ginger for **2 min**.
4. Add the tomato paste, blended tomatoes, cardamom, ground spices and salt. Cook **8–10 min**, stirring, until thick and the oil separates; splash in water if it sticks.
5. Off the heat, let it cool **5 min**, fish out the cardamom, and blend it smooth (blender or food processor, **1 min**). Back into the pot with the 400 ml water and the sugar if needed.
6. **Medium:** bring to a bubble, add the peas, lid ajar, **6 min**. Add the paneer and simmer lid off **10 min**, stirring gently so the cubes stay whole, until they soften and take on the sauce. Add a splash of water if it dries out.
7. Stir in the cream and bring back just to a simmer. Off the heat: garam masala and coriander. Taste for salt.

sections.title: Ingredients (22 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Eggplants (bedenjal) | ~8 medium (2.5 kg) | 1.5 cm rounds |
| Salt, for drawing out the water | 1 tbsp | |
| Oil | 6 tbsp (80 g) for the trays + 1 tbsp (15 g) for the sauce | |
| Garlic (thoum) | 5 cloves (25 g) | crushed |
| Caraway (karwiya), sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tsp each | |
| Black pepper | ½ tsp | |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 60 g (2½ tbsp) | |
| Tomatoes (tmatem) | 3 (~400 g) | grated, skins thrown away |
| Chickpeas (hommos), canned or home-cooked | 1 can, drained (~240 g) | |
| Water | 300 ml | |
| White vinegar (khal) | 2 tbsp (30 ml) | |
| Sugar | 1½ tbsp (20 g) | |
| Egg | 1 | |
| Breadcrumbs (chapelure) | 2 tbsp (20 g) | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Salt the eggplant:** layer the slices in a colander with the salt and leave **30 min** to drain. Pat them dry with a clean towel.
2. **Oven 220 °C.** Brush the slices on both sides with the 80 g oil and lay them on parchment-lined trays in one layer. Roast **25 min**, turning at 15 min, until soft and golden.
3. **Sauce, wide pot, low heat:** 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, caraway, paprika and pepper for **1 min**, stirring so the garlic softens without browning. Add the tomato paste for 1 min, then the grated tomatoes, chickpeas and 300 ml water. Simmer **15 min**.
4. Stir in the vinegar and sugar and taste: it should be gently sweet-sour and well salted (the eggplant carries some salt already). Lay the roasted eggplant in and simmer **5 min**.
5. **The finish:** take a ladle of sauce, let it cool for 2–3 min, then whisk in the egg and breadcrumbs. Pour it back into the pot and stir gently. Simmer **3–4 min**, stirring, until the sauce thickens and there's no runny egg left.
6. It should be thick and saucy, not soupy; if it's thin, simmer a few minutes more with the lid off. Cool **30 min**.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **22**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **125 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir; white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. **Burner 1, pan, medium:** oil, onion and pepper with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft with no raw bite. Garlic for the last minute. Spread on a plate to cool for 10 min.
2. **Oven 200 °C.** In a big bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 min, then beat in the eggs, mustard, paprika, thyme, pepper and salt.
3. Add the mince, the cooled onion mix and the parsley. Mix with your hands **just until even**; over-mixing makes them dense.
4. Lightly oil **14 silicone muffin cups** set on a tray. Fill each with a scoop (~105 g), pressing it in and smoothing the top.
5. Stir the glaze together and spread a teaspoonful over each.
6. Bake **22–25 min**, until the glaze is sticky and the middle reaches 71 °C (no pink; clear juices). Rest 5 min, then pour off any fat and pop them out.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **7 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:
1. **Potatoes:** slices in a bowl with 3 tbsp water, covered, **microwave 6–7 min** until just tender. Drain.
2. **Big frying pan, medium heat:** olive oil and onion with a pinch of salt for **8 min** until soft. Add the garlic, peppers and zucchini for **8–10 min**, until the pan is dry and the zucchini is lightly browned. Stir in the spinach for **2 min**. Cool 10 min.
3. **Oven 180 °C.** Oil a **30 × 40 cm** deep oven tray and line the base with parchment. Lay the potato slices over the base, overlapping.
4. Whisk the eggs, milk, oregano, salt and pepper. Stir in the veg, olives, feta, two-thirds of the fromage rouge and the parsley. Pour over the potatoes and scatter the rest of the cheese on top.
5. Bake **35–40 min**, until puffed, golden and set in the middle (a knife comes out clean). Don't overbake or it goes rubbery.
6. Cool **15 min**, then cut into **15 squares** (3 × 5).


**Prepare for cubes:** For an egg or oat bake, crumble or cut the cooked soft mixture into small pieces and press into the cube mold while warm. Porridge can be spooned in directly. Freeze only after the egg or batter is fully cooked; a breakfast cube should be moist, not a crisp pastry.

- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method.
2. **8 L pot on medium,** meanwhile: oil and onions for **5 min**. Add the carrots, celery and pepper and cook **10–12 min**, stirring, until the celery is soft.
3. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and oregano for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for 1 min and the tomatoes for **5 min**, until they collapse into a thick salsa.
4. Add the beans, the 1 L of bean water, **800 ml water**, the stock cubes and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer **15 min**, **stirring the bottom often** (beans catch and burn).
5. Fish out the bay leaves. **Blend about a third:** ladle roughly 1.5 L into a blender (filled no more than half, lid vented, towel on top), blend smooth and stir it back in. Or give the pot a few pulses with a stick blender.
6. Add the corn and simmer **3 min**. **Off the heat:** lemon juice and coriander; taste for salt and pepper.
7. It should be thick but still pour from the ladle. Loosen with a little boiling water if it's stiff.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté (or heavy pot), medium-high:** 30 ml oil, brown the beef strips in 2 rounds, **3–4 min** a round. Lift out.
2. **Medium:** 15 ml oil and onion **5 min** until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric and cinnamon **1 min**.
3. Add the tomato, sugar, salt, peppers and carrots and the beef. **Lid on, high pressure 25 min**, natural release 10 min. Pot: lid on, simmer **1 h 30 min**.
4. Stir in the peas and cream and simmer **4–5 min**, lid off, until thick. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:
1. **Wide pot, medium:** oil, onion and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic for **1 min**; don't let it brown (brown garlic makes the sauce bitter).
2. Stir in the flour and cook **1 min** into a paste. Turn the heat low and stir in the paprikas, cumin and oregano for **30 s**, then the tomato paste for **1 min**.
3. Pour in a ladle of the hot stock, scraping the bottom and stirring until smooth, then the rest of the stock and the chopped tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then **medium-low, lid ajar, 25 min**, stirring every 5 min.
4. **Blend** with a stick blender (or in batches in the blender, with a cloth over the lid and the vent open) until completely smooth. Taste: add the sugar if it's sharp, plus salt and pepper. If it's thinner than ketchup, simmer lid off for 5–10 min more.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. - Produce: use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Night before:** soak each type of dried bean separately in cold water in the fridge.
2. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method. Keep 500 ml bean cooking water.
3. **8 L pot on medium,** while the beans cook: olive oil, onion and leek for **6 min** until soft. Add the garlic for 1 min, then the carrots, celery and red pepper for **5 min**.
4. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 min. Add the tomatoes, zucchini and green beans, lid on, and let them sweat **10 min**, stirring now and then.
5. Add the potatoes, the cooked beans and their 500 ml of water, **1 L water**, the stock cubes and the herbs. Simmer, lid ajar, **20 min**, until the potatoes are tender.
6. Add the peas for **5 min**.
7. **Off the heat:** stir in the fromage rouge, basil and lemon juice; fish out the rosemary sprig and bay leaves. Taste for salt and pepper.
8. It should be thick and chunky, with enough broth to ladle. Top up with a little boiling water if you're well under 5 L.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Rub the beef with the ranch mix and the flour.
2. **Pressure cooker on sauté, high:** oil, then brown the beef **3 min a side**. Lift out. Onions in for **3 min**, then pour in the stock and scrape the bottom clean.
3. Beef back in, carrots around it, then the gherkins and brine. Dot the butter on top of the beef. Don't stir.
4. **Lid on, high pressure 60 min**, natural release 15 min (the source's timing). Slow cooker instead: everything in after step 2, **low 8 h**.
5. Lift the beef onto a board and shred it with two forks. If the gravy is thin, **sauté, lid off, 5 min**. Beef back in with the fresh dill and parsley and stir well. Taste: the pickles and stock are salty, so add salt only if it needs it.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drained soaked chickpeas, fresh water to 3 cm above, a pinch of salt, **no more than half full**. **High pressure 15 min**, natural release 15 min, until tender. Drain.
2. **Dersa:** pound the garlic, cumin and 1 tsp salt to a paste in a mortar (or crush on the board with the flat of a knife), then loosen with 2 tbsp water.
3. **Heavy pot, medium:** olive oil, bay leaf and onion for **8 min**, until soft. Add the dersa and the tomato paste and cook **3–4 min**, stirring and watching closely, until the oil starts to rise to the surface. Don't let it burn; add a splash of water if it catches.
4. Stir in the paprikas, turmeric, curry powder and cinnamon for **30 s**, then the blended tomatoes, sweet potato, chickpeas and the 200 ml stock. Bring to a boil, lid on, simmer **20 min**, until the sweet potato is tender. Taste; add the sugar only if it's sharp.
5. Lid off. Smash a few sweet potato cubes and a spoon of chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken it. Add the olives and spinach and simmer **5 min** more, stirring, until the spinach has wilted and the sauce is thick.
6. Off the heat: parsley, black pepper and a pinch of cumin. Fish out the bay leaf and taste for salt (the olives and dersa are already salty).

sections.content:

- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C.** Line 3 trays with parchment. Lay the eggplant slices on 2 trays and the potato slices on the third, brush both sides with the oil and sprinkle with salt. Roast **20–25 min**, until the eggplant is soft and golden and a knife slides through the potato. Leave the oven on.
2. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium heat** (while the veg roasts): 1 tsp oil, onions and a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Turn up, add the **beef** and break it up for **6–8 min**, until no pink is left. Add the garlic, ground cinnamon and oregano for 1 min, then the tomato paste for 1 min.
3. Add the grated tomatoes, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer with the lid off for **20 min**, stirring now and then, until **thick with no pool of liquid** (a watery sauce makes soggy tubs). Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay.
4. **Burner 2, béchamel:** melt the butter on medium-low, stir in the flour and cook **2 min**. Off the heat, pour in the milk a splash at a time, whisking. Back on medium, whisking, **5–6 min** until thick like custard. Add the nutmeg and salt. Let it cool **5 min**, then whisk in the eggs and half the cheese (hot béchamel scrambles the eggs).
5. **Build it** in the oven dish: potato slices over the bottom, **half the eggplant**, all the meat sauce, the rest of the eggplant, then the béchamel spread to the edges, and the rest of the cheese.
6. **Bake 30–35 min**, until the top is set and golden in patches.
7. **Rest 15 min** so it sets and cuts cleanly, then cut into 6.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Pressure cooker on sauté, medium:** smen, oil and grated onion for **5 min** until soft. Add the pounded garlic for **1–2 min**, stirring, until it smells sweet but hasn't browned.
2. Add the cinnamon stick, thyme, pepper, salt, the drained chickpeas and the **1.2 litres boiling water**. **Lid on, high pressure 20 min**, natural release 10 min. With canned chickpeas, skip the pressure: simmer the sauce 15 min and add the chickpeas with the meatballs.
3. **Meatballs, while it cooks:** mix everything for the meatballs with your hands until sticky and even. Roll about **42 small balls** (~25 g) with wet hands.
4. Open the pot, bring the sauce back to a lively simmer (sauté, or a burner), and drop the meatballs in one at a time. Simmer **uncovered 20 min**, shaking the pot now and then, until they're cooked through and the sauce has reduced by about a third. Taste for salt. Fish out the cinnamon stick.

sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Coconut milk is an optional shopping dependency: for each **100 ml**, use **75 ml whole milk + 25 ml cooking cream** if unavailable. Stir this alternative in near the end and heat gently; the sauce will be lighter and lose its coconut flavour.
- Lentilles corail dissolve into the sauce. If only brown/green adas are available, cook them separately until soft before adding, then blend or mash if a smooth texture is needed; the same dry weight will have a different cooking time.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot on medium-high:** 1 tbsp oil and the chicken in two batches, **4 min** each, until fully cooked (74 °C). Transfer to a clean shallow bowl and refrigerate promptly while making the soup.
2. Same pot, medium: the rest of the oil, the onions and carrots for **8 min**, scraping up the brown bits, until soft.
3. Turn to low. Add the garlic, ginger and all the dry spices for **1 min**, stirring (curry powder scorches fast).
4. Add the apples, tomatoes, lentils, stock cubes and **2.4 L water**. Bring to the boil, then simmer uncovered **30 min**, stirring the bottom now and then, until the lentils and carrots are completely soft.
5. **Blend until smooth** with a stick blender, or in a blender in batches filled no more than half, lid vented and a towel on top.
6. Back on the heat: add the chicken and any juices. Simmer **10 min**; cut the biggest piece open: check it reaches 74 °C.
7. Stir in the coconut milk and heat **2 min** without a hard boil. Off the heat, add the lemon juice and coriander, and taste for salt.
8. It should pour like thick cream. If it's thicker than that, loosen with a little boiling water.

label: MUSH BARLEY
portion: 1/10 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: rice or mash cubes; add a chicken cube if more protein is needed
photoTitle: Mushroom Barley Soup, a Jewish Version

sections.title: Ingredients (10 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Oil | 3 tbsp (30 ml) | |
| Mushrooms (champignons de Paris) | 1.2 kg | thickly sliced |
| Onions (basal) | 1½ (~250 g) | chopped |
| Carrots (zroudiya) | 2–3 (~250 g) | coins |
| Celery (krafes) | 1 stalk with leaves (~100 g) | chopped |
| Garlic (thoum) | 4 cloves (20 g) | crushed |
| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 40 g | |
| Canned tomatoes (tomate pelée) | 1 × 400 g can | crushed with a spoon (or 400 g fresh, grated) |
| Brown lentils (adas) | 550 g | rinsed and picked over |
| Pearl barley (chaïr / orge perlé) | 180 g | rinsed |
| Bay leaves (laurier), dried thyme (zaâtar) | 2, 1 tsp | |
| Soy sauce (sauce soja) | 1 tbsp (20 g) | |
| Beef, chicken or vegetable stock cubes | 3 | |
| Water | 2.6 L | |
| Fresh dill (aneth / shebt) | 1 bunch (~30 g) | chopped |
| Parsley (maadnous) | small handful (20 g) | chopped |
| Salt, black pepper | to taste | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce; use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Ask for orge perlé, hulled/pearled barley. Dchicha is cracked barley: it is a possible same-dry-weight variant, but thickens and cooks faster; follow its texture and add water gradually.
- Seasoning alternatives: parsley replaces dill by the same fresh or dried quantity.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot, high:** 2 tbsp oil and the mushrooms, in two batches if the pot is crowded, for **10–12 min**, stirring now and then, until their water has cooked off and they're browned. This is where the flavour comes from, so don't rush it. Scoop them out into a bowl.
2. **Medium heat:** the last 1 tbsp oil, onions, carrots and celery for **7 min**, until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste for **2 min**.
3. Add the canned tomatoes, lentils, barley, bay, thyme, soy sauce, stock cubes and **2.6 L water**, scraping up the brown bits. Bring to the boil, then lid half on and simmer **40–45 min**, stirring every 10 min (barley sticks), until the barley is chewy-tender and the lentils are soft.
4. Stir the mushrooms back in for the last **5 min**. Off the heat, fish out the bay leaves and add the dill and parsley. Taste for salt and pepper.
5. **Leave it a little looser than you'd serve it**: barley and lentils keep drinking liquid in the freezer. If it's already porridge-thick, stir in up to 300 ml boiling water.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.
