name: Oat and peanut dessert cubes
label: OAT AND PEANUT DESSERT CUBES
portion: 1/15 of batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: compatible dessert cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (15 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Rolled oats (flocons d'avoine) | 300 g | |
| Puffed rice (riz soufflé) | 120 g | |
| Roasted peanuts, unsalted (cacahuètes grillées) | 60 g | roughly chopped |
| Honey (asal / miel) | 120 g | |
| Brown sugar (cassonade) | 80 g | |
| Butter (beurre) | 30 g | |
| Salt | ½ tsp | |
| Peanut butter (beurre de cacahuète) | 200 g | |
| Vanilla sugar (sucre vanillé) | 1 sachet (8 g) | |
| Dark chocolate (chocolat noir pâtissier) | 50 g | chopped small |

No puffed rice? Use lightly crushed cornflakes, same weight.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Épicerie alternatives: unsweetened peanut butter can be made by processing roasted unsalted cacahuètes until smooth; weigh the paste needed; white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- If puffed rice is unavailable, use the same weight of roughly crushed plain cornflakes; press into the oat mixture. Check that the cereal is not heavily sweetened.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Line a 20 × 30 cm tray** with baking paper, with an overhang on the long sides.
2. In a big bowl, mix the oats, puffed rice and chopped peanuts.
3. **Syrup**, one burner, medium heat, in a saucepan: honey, brown sugar, butter and salt. Bring to a boil, stirring, and **boil 1 min** exactly (longer and the bars go hard; shorter and they crumble).
4. Off the heat, stir in the peanut butter and vanilla sugar until smooth.
5. Pour it over the dry mix and stir until every flake is coated. Leave **5 min** to firm up a little.
6. Tip it into the tray and **press it down very hard and flat** with the base of a glass or a second tray; firm pressing is what holds the bars together. Scatter the chocolate over and press again so it sticks (it melts a little into the warm top).
7. **Fridge 1 h** until firm, lift out and cut into **15 bars** (3 × 5) with a big sharp knife.


**Cube version:** instead of forming balls or cutting bars, press the completed mixtures into 60 ml molds, including their chocolate or nut layers. Keep any different flavours separate. Never add uncooked flour; the oat and nut ingredients here are ready to eat.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **15 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **60 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **No reheat:** eat directly from the freezer as a cold component, allowing 5–10 min to soften if needed. Combine with compatible cold breakfast or dessert cubes, serve immediately and do not refreeze the softened portion.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 220 °C.** Toss the okra with 30 g oil and ½ tsp salt and spread it in one layer on 2 parchment-lined trays. Roast **20–25 min** (frozen: **25–30 min**), shaking once, until lightly browned and no longer sticky.
2. **Sauce, heavy pot, medium heat, meanwhile:** 20 g oil and the onion for **3–4 min**, until soft. Add the cardamom for 30 s, then the tomato paste, stirring often for **2–3 min** until it darkens.
3. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, garam masala, coriander and cumin and cook **2 min**, stirring; it's fine if the bottom browns a little.
4. Add the crushed tomatoes with their juice and the rest of the salt, scraping the bottom, and simmer **10 min**.
5. Stir in the cream and simmer uncovered for **30 min**, stirring now and then, until thick and rich.
6. Fold in the roasted okra and simmer **3–4 min**. Taste for salt. Cool **30 min**.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:

- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles; choose firm pizza mozzarella; the same weight of grated fromage rouge works with less stretch.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Big pot, medium-high:** oil, then the chicken with ½ tsp salt. Cook **6–7 min**, stirring now and then, until white all over and browned in places. It finishes cooking with the pasta.
2. Medium heat. Add the onion and peppers for **5 min** until softened. Add the garlic, paprikas, thyme, oregano and pepper for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for **1 min**.
3. Add the canned tomatoes and **1 L of stock**, scrape the bottom, and bring to the boil.
4. Stir in the **penne**, bring back to a boil, then turn to a lively simmer, lid off. Cook **10–11 min**, **stirring every 2 min** so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is **just al dente** (1–2 min less than the packet). Add a splash of water if it gets thick before the pasta is ready.
5. Stir in the spinach for **1 min** until wilted.
6. **Heat off.** Stir in the cream, then the mozzarella and fromage rouge until melted. Taste for salt. It should look **saucier than you'd serve it**; the pasta drinks the sauce as it cools and freezes.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C.** Spread the onion over the bottom of a big roasting dish. Whisk the orange juice, zest, garlic, ginger, cumin, oil, honey, soy, Dijon, salt and pepper, pour half over the onions and turn the thighs in the rest. Lay the thighs on the onions and pour over the remaining marinade.
2. **Bake uncovered 35–40 min**, spooning the juices over at 20 min, until golden and the thickest thigh is 74 °C (juices clear).
3. Lift the thighs onto a board and cut into 3–4 cm chunks. **Scrape all the juices and onions into a pot on burner 1, medium,** add the tomatoes and **simmer 8 min**.
4. Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer **2 min** until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Chicken back in, with the herbs. Taste: a squeeze of orange or a pinch of salt if flat.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Meatballs:** mix everything under "Meatballs" with your hands (or pulse onion, herbs and garlic in a food processor first, then add the rest and pulse 20–30 s). Don't overmix. With oiled hands roll **42 balls** (~28 g, the size of a walnut) and lay them on a tray. Chill while you make the sauce.
2. **Burner 1, big wide pot, medium-high:** oil, then the whole spices and cumin seeds for a few seconds. Add the onions and stir for **8 min** until golden brown. Add a splash of water if they catch.
3. Add the garlic and ginger for **2 min**, then the tomato, yogurt, ground spices and salt. Stir for **5–6 min**, until the oil starts to separate from the sauce.
4. Add **600 ml water**, bring to a boil, then lower the heat until it stops boiling.
5. Lay the meatballs in one layer in the sauce (2 rounds if your pot is small; the first round can stay in the pot while the second goes on top once it has firmed). Don't stir yet.
6. **Medium heat, lid on, 10 min.** Then stir gently, lower the heat, lid on and simmer **35 min**, stirring once, until cooked through (74 °C in the middle of a ball).
7. Lid off, **5–10 min** to reduce to a thick sauce that coats a spoon. Stir in the garam masala and coriander, and taste for salt. Take out the bay leaves, cinnamon and cardamom pods if you can see them; the cloves can stay.

sections.content:

- Make paneer from fresh pasteurized whole milk if available. UHT success and yield vary, so try 250 ml first. The nutrition assumes 480 g drained cheese, not all the nutrients in the starting milk; press and chill promptly. [Paneer technique](https://cheesemaking.com/pages/paneer-cheese-making-recipe-instructions).

- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Paneer, the evening before (big pot, medium-high):** heat the milk gently to 85–90 °C, stirring so it does not catch. Off the heat, pour in the vinegar-water a little at a time, stirring gently, until the curds separate and the whey turns clear and yellow-green (you may not need all of it). Rest **5 min**.
2. Line a colander with a clean thin cloth and pour in the curds. Rinse with cold water to wash off the vinegar taste, gather the cloth and squeeze out the whey. Flatten into a 2 cm slab, still in the cloth, put a board and a heavy pot of water on top, and press **1 h in the fridge**, using a clean weighted container. Aim for **480 g of drained paneer**, but weigh the yield: milk type changes it. If short, make another small batch or recalculate for the amount actually used. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
3. **Curry, wide pot, medium-high:** oil, then the cumin seeds and onion for **10 min**, until golden brown. Deglaze with 2 tbsp water. Add the garlic and ginger for **2 min**.
4. Add the tomato, ground spices, paprika and salt, and cook **4–5 min**, until the oil separates from the sauce.
5. Turn up the heat and add the spinach a handful at a time, cooking about **5 min** until wilted. Lid on, medium heat, **10 min**, stirring once.
6. Off the heat, cool **5 min**, then purée roughly in a blender or food processor (20 pulses, **1 min**): it should stay a little textured, not a smooth paste.
7. Back in the pot on medium-high: butter, then the purée for **1 min**. Add **150 ml water**, stir.
8. Add the paneer, milk and cream. **Low-medium, lid on, 8–10 min**, stirring gently so the cubes stay whole, until the paneer has softened and taken on the sauce and the oil shows at the edges.
9. Crumble in the fenugreek leaves, add the lemon and the garam masala, and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinade:** blend all the marinade ingredients until smooth, **1 min**. Pour it over the drumsticks in a big bowl, massage it into the slashes, cover and chill for **2 h** (or overnight). The onion and garlic in it cook through on the tray.
2. **Oven 200 °C** (fan 180 °C). Line 2 large trays with parchment (3 if they're small). Toss the potatoes, peppers and onion wedges with the olive oil, ½ tsp salt and 2 tbsp of the marinade.
3. **Spread the vegetables** over the trays and sit the drumsticks among them, spooning the rest of the marinade over the chicken. One layer, nothing piled up.
4. **Roast 25 min**, then turn the drumsticks, stir the potatoes and swap the trays. Roast **20–25 min more**. It's done when a knife slides into the biggest wedge, the potatoes are golden at the edges, and the thickest drumstick reads 74 °C next to the bone. For crisper skin, 3 min under the grill at the end.
5. Scatter the parsley over.


**Prepare for cubes:** After cooking, remove every bone and piece of cartilage and chop or shred the meat to 1–2 cm. Mix it with the cooked sauce and juices before filling molds; no bones go into a cube. For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C.** Big pot of salted water on to boil (**burner 1**).
2. **Burner 2, wide pot, medium heat:** oil, onion, carrot and a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft with no raw bite. Turn up, add the **beef** and break it up for **6–8 min**, until no pink is left. Add the garlic, cinnamon, nutmeg, fennel and oregano for 1 min, then the tomato paste for 1 min.
3. Add the grated tomatoes, stock, sugar, bay, salt and pepper. Simmer with the lid off for **20 min**, until **thick with no pool of liquid**. Stir in the lemon juice and fish out the bay.
4. **Burner 1:** cook the pasta for **3 min less than the packet says** (it finishes in the oven). Drain.
5. **Burner 3, béchamel:** melt the butter on medium-low, stir in the flour for **2 min**. Off the heat, whisk in the milk a splash at a time. Back on medium, whisking, **5–6 min** until thick like custard. Season with nutmeg and salt. Cool **5 min**, then whisk in the eggs and **50 g** of the cheese.
6. Toss the drained pasta with **3 big spoons of the béchamel** (it holds the pasta layer together when you cut it).
7. **Build it** in the oven dish: half the pasta, all the meat sauce, the rest of the pasta, then the rest of the béchamel spread to the edges and the last 20 g of cheese on top.
8. **Bake 30 min**, until set and golden in patches. **Rest 15 min**, then cut into 6.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Crush all the plain petit beurre biscuits finely. Melt the butter and mix with the biscuits.
2. Whisk unsweetened fromage blanc, plain yogurt, icing sugar, vanilla sugar and peanut butter smooth. Whip the cold 30% cream to soft peaks, then fold it in along with the biscuit mixture and pinch of salt.
3. Spoon the complete dessert mixture into 60 ml molds and freeze promptly. It is a frozen dessert cube, not a baked cake; use plain biscuits and homemade peanut butter rather than depending on Lotus products.

2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Coconut milk is an optional shopping dependency: for each **100 ml**, use **75 ml whole milk + 25 ml cooking cream** if unavailable. Stir this alternative in near the end and heat gently; the sauce will be lighter and lose its coconut flavour.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir; unsweetened peanut butter can be made by processing roasted unsalted cacahuètes until smooth; weigh the paste needed.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium:** oil and onion for **6–8 min** until soft. Garlic and ginger for 1 min, then the pepper for 3 min. Stir in the cumin and coriander for 30 seconds.
2. Whisk the peanut butter with about 100 ml of the hot stock until smooth (it stops it clumping), then whisk in the rest of the stock, the coconut milk, soy, honey and pepper. Pour into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Add the chicken and **simmer 10–12 min**, stirring now and then, until the thickest cube is 74 °C and white all through. Don't boil hard: it can split the coconut and scorch the peanut butter.
4. Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer **2 min** until glossy and thick. Off the heat, add the lemon juice and taste: more soy if flat, a little lemon if heavy.
5. Stir in the crushed peanuts last so they keep a bit of crunch.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, big pot:** 3 L of water and 1 tbsp salt to the boil. Tip in the barley and simmer for **5 min less than the packet says** (usually **25–30 min**). It should be tender with a firm bite in the middle. Drain it.
2. **Burner 2, wide pot, medium heat** (while the barley cooks): oil, onions, carrots and a pinch of salt for **10 min**, until the onion is soft and golden with no raw bite.
3. Turn up to medium-high. Add the **beef** and break it up with a wooden spoon for **6–8 min**, until there's no pink left and its liquid has cooked off. Add the garlic, cumin, coriander and paprika and stir for **1 min**.
4. Stir in the tomato paste for **1 min**, then the grated tomatoes and the **500 ml stock**. Simmer with the lid off for **10 min**.
5. Add the peas and cook **3 min**.
6. Tip in the drained barley, stir well, and give it **5 min on low**. Taste for salt and pepper, and stir in the herbs.
7. It should look **looser than you'd serve it**, like a wet risotto. The barley keeps soaking up sauce as it cools and freezes, so if it's already thick, stir in 100–200 ml of hot water.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Burner 1, big pot, medium:** oil, onions and peppers with a pinch of salt for **8–10 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Garlic for 1 min.
2. Add the mince, break it into small clumps and brown for **8–10 min**. Spoon off pooled fat.
3. Stir in the spices and tomato paste for **2 min**.
4. Add the passata, water, stock cube, potatoes and raisins. Bring to a simmer, **lid on, low heat, 20–25 min**, stirring now and then, until the potato dice are just tender and the sauce is thick (lid off for the last 5 min if it's wet).
5. Off the heat, stir in the coriander. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

2. **Two big pots, medium heat:** 5 g butter in each and **425 g oats** in each. Stir for **2 min** until they smell nutty (toasting them keeps the texture after freezing).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Beans, pressure cooker:** drain the soaked beans, add **1.2 L fresh water** (no salt yet), **high pressure 10 min**, natural release 15 min. They should crush easily. Keep them in their cooking water. (Pot instead: simmer 1 h–1 h 15 min. Canned: rinse them and use 1.2 L more water in step 3.)
2. **8 L pot, medium-low:** the butter, oil, leeks and onion with a pinch of salt, lid on, for **12–15 min**, stirring now and then, until very soft but not browned. Add the garlic for 1 min.
3. Add the potatoes, the beans with all their cooking water, the stock cubes, bay, thyme and **800 ml water**. Bring to the boil, then lid on and simmer **20 min**, until the potatoes fall apart when poked.
4. Fish out the bay leaves. Scoop out 2 ladles of potato cubes and set them aside. Blend the rest until completely smooth, in batches in the blender (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender).
5. Back in the pot on low: stir in the milk, lben and the reserved potatoes and heat until it just steams, **3–4 min**. Don't let it boil, or the lben splits. Off the heat, stir in the fromage rouge, nutmeg, pepper and parsley, and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

| Flour (farine) | 1 heaped tbsp (15 g) | |
| Ground coriander, sweet paprika (paprika doux) | ½ tsp each | |
| Chicken stock cube | 1 | dissolved in 250 ml hot water |
| Dried thyme (zaâtar), bay leaves (laurier) | 1 tsp, 2 | |
| Dijon mustard (moutarde) | 4 tbsp (60 g) | |
| Crème fraîche (crème fraîche épaisse) | 150 g | |
| Parsley (maadnous) | small handful | chopped |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Épicerie alternatives: use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Rub the chicken with the ginger, garlic, salt and pepper, as she does.
2. **Burner 1, wide pot, medium-high:** melt half the butter until it foams and starts to colour, then sear the strips in 2–3 batches, **2 min a side**, until golden. Add a little more butter per batch. Lift them onto a plate; they finish cooking later.
3. Heat to medium. Onion into the pot with the last of the butter for **8 min**, scraping up the brown bits, until soft and golden. Stir in the flour, coriander and paprika for 1 min.
4. Whisk in the **hot stock** a little at a time, add the thyme and bay, and simmer **3 min** until thickened. Return the chicken and its juices and **simmer 5–6 min**, until the thickest strip is 74 °C.
5. **Off the heat**, let it stop bubbling (1–2 min), then stir in the Dijon and crème fraîche. Boiling now would split the cream and dull the mustard. Fish out the bay, add the parsley and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Pan, medium:** oil and onion **6 min** until soft and translucent with no raw bite. Add the garlic, cumin and paprika **1 min**. Cool 10 min.
2. Mash the beans roughly with a fork or pulse in a food processor (keep some texture). Mix with the onion, eggs, salt, pepper and breadcrumbs.
3. Chill the mix **30–40 min** so it firms. Shape **12 patties**, 9 cm across and 1.5 cm thick.
4. **Oven to 200 °C.** Line 2 trays with oiled baking paper. **Bake 25 min**, turning once at 12 min, until firm and browned on both sides.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **8 L pot on medium:** olive oil, onion, leek, celery and red pepper for **6–7 min**, stirring, until soft and translucent. If they catch, add a spoon of water rather than more oil.
2. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika, black pepper and tomato paste. Stir for **1 min**.

5. Add the diced chicken and simmer **10–12 min**. Cut the biggest piece open: white all through, no pink.
6. For a creamier body, crush a few pieces of sweet potato against the side of the pot and stir. Add the parsley and taste for salt and pepper.
7. Leave it a little looser than you'd serve it: the lentils keep thickening in the freezer.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Rice (burner 1):** boil in plenty of salted water with the turmeric and cardamom for **10–11 min** until just tender. Drain very well and fish out the cardamom.
2. **Zucchini (burner 2, big frying pan):** 1 tsp oil, the grated zucchini and a pinch of salt on medium-high for **8–10 min**, stirring, until the water has cooked off and it looks soft and dry. Wet zucchini makes a soggy gratin.
3. **Chicken (burner 3):** 1 tbsp oil, the chicken and the spice mix on medium-high for **5 min**, then add **2 tbsp crème fraîche** and cook **5 min more**, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has reduced to a coating.
4. **Oven on at 180 °C.** In a big bowl, mix the rice, zucchini and chicken with its sauce. Stir in the eggs, the rest of the crème fraîche and **120 g cheese**.
5. Oil your largest oven dish, tip the mix in and press it level. **Bake 20 min**, until set in the middle (a knife comes out clean, with no runny egg).
6. Scatter the last **60 g cheese** over and bake **10 min more** until golden.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C.** Spread the tomatoes (cut side up), onions, carrots and garlic over 2–3 trays in a single layer. Drizzle with the oil, season with the salt and pepper, and roast **45–60 min**, until soft and browned at the edges. Swap the trays halfway.
2. **Meanwhile, 8 L pot, medium-high:** the lentils, tomato paste, stock cubes, thyme, bay and **1.6 L water**. Bring to the boil, skim off the foam, then simmer **15–20 min**, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed.
3. Squeeze the garlic out of its skins. Tip everything from the trays, juices included, into the pot. Simmer **10 min**. Fish out the bay leaves and add the basil.
4. Blend until completely smooth, in batches in the blender (fill it only halfway and vent the lid as the manufacturer permits; never seal a hot mixture in a closed blender; hot soup pushes the lid off).
5. Back in the pot on low, stir in the milk and heat until it just steams, **3–4 min**, without letting it boil hard. Taste: salt, pepper, and the sugar if it's sharp. It should coat a spoon; it thickens more in the freezer.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- If lait concentré non sucré is unavailable, gently reduce **2 ml whole milk to 1 ml** needed, then measure the reduced amount before use. Sweetened condensed milk is unsuitable for this savoury dish.
- Produce: champignons may be fresh or plain canned, using the listed weight after draining; dry-fry drained ones briefly before adding sauce.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour; use mild prepared moutarde made without added alcohol, and reduce it to taste if the jar is sharp; check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 200 °C**, two trays lined with parchment.
2. **Patties:** mix everything for the patties with your hands until even. Divide into **14** (~80 g each) and shape ovals about 1.5 cm thick, small enough that two fit side by side or stacked in a 250 ml tub. **Bake 15 min** until browned; they finish cooking in the gravy.
3. **Gravy, while they bake:** wide pot on medium. Butter and onions with a pinch of salt for **10–12 min**, stirring now and then, until soft and golden. Add the mushrooms for **5–6 min** until their liquid cooks off.
4. Sprinkle over the flour and stir for **1 min**. Pour in the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring out lumps, then the evaporated milk, ketchup, soy, thyme and pepper. Simmer **5 min** until it coats a spoon.
5. Lay the patties in the gravy (overlapping is fine) with their juices. Lid on and simmer gently for **10 min**, spooning gravy over them, until the middle of a patty is no longer pink (71 °C).


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Balls:** chop the sardine fillets fine in a food processor (short pulses, not a paste). Mix with the rice, coriander, half the garlic, half the cumin, the mint, pepper and 1 tsp of the salt. Cover and chill **20 min**.

3. With wet hands, roll the sardine mix into **24 balls** (~35 g each).
4. Turn the heat to low. Lower the balls into the sauce in one layer, **lid on, 15 min**, without stirring (shake the pot gently if you need to move them). They're done when firm and opaque right through, with no raw pink.

sections.content:

- Use the dairy fat level listed: crème cuisson around 20% and crème fraîche épaisse around 30% are different. For a milk alternative to 100 ml cream in a sauce, use 100 ml milk mixed cold with 3 g Maïzena, then simmer gently until thick; this changes the figures.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Beans, pressure cooker:** drain the soaked beans, add **1.2 L fresh water**, **high pressure 10 min**, natural release 15 min. Keep them in their cooking water. (Pot instead: simmer 1 h–1 h 15 min. Canned: rinse them and use 1.2 L more water in step 4.)
2. **Sausage mix:** in a bowl, work the fennel seed, paprika, oregano, garlic powder, salt and pepper into the mince with your hands.
3. **8 L pot, medium-high:** the oil and the mince for **8–10 min**, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned with no pink left. Add the onions and carrots for **6 min**, then the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for **2 min**.
4. Add the beans with all their cooking water, the stock cubes, bay, potatoes and **1 L water**. Bring to the boil, then lid half on and simmer **15 min**. Add the zucchini for **8–10 min more**, until the potatoes are tender.
5. Off the heat, fish out the bay leaves and stir in the cream and parsley. Crush a ladle of beans and potato against the side of the pot to thicken the broth a little. Taste for salt and pepper.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

2. Oil a **30 × 40 cm** deep oven tray (or two 20 × 30 cm dishes). Spread in the bread, then the meat mix and two-thirds of the cheese, and toss lightly so it's mixed through.

5. Cool **15 min**, then cut into **15 squares** (3 × 5).

sections.title: Ingredients (6 recipe servings)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Beef mince (viande hachée) | 1 kg | ask for it "pas trop maigre" if you can; drain and pat dry |
| Butter (beurre) | 25 g | soft |
| Onion (basal) | 1 small (~120 g) | roughly chopped |
| Fresh coriander (kosbor) | ¼ bunch (~25 g) | leaves and thin stems |
| Fresh mint (naânaâ) | a small handful (~8 g) | leaves |
| Garlic (thoum) | 5 cloves (25 g) | crushed |
| Ginger (skinjbir) | a 4 cm piece (15 g) | grated |
| Coriander seeds and cumin seeds (kammoun) | 1½ tbsp each | toasted and ground (step 1) |
| Garam masala | 2 tsp | or ½ tsp each of cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and black pepper |
| Black pepper (felfel k'hal) | 2 tsp | |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tsp | |
| Salt | 1½ tsp | |
| Lemon juice (citron) | 1 tbsp | |
| Oil | 1 tbsp | for brushing |

Chicken version: 1 kg chicken thigh mince works the same way. It's wetter, so squeeze the onion extra dry and add 2 tbsp of chickpea flour or breadcrumbs (chapelure) if the mix won't hold.


**Additional sauce for the cube version**

| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| Crushed tomatoes (tomates pelées) | 600 g |
| Halal stock cube | 1 (10 g), dissolved in 250 ml water |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Keep the additional tomato and stock sauce ingredients aside while preparing the meat mixture; they are used only in the final sauce step.


1. **Burner 1, small dry pan, medium:** toast the coriander and cumin seeds for **2–3 min**, shaking, until darker and fragrant. Cool for 5 min and grind (spice grinder, or a mortar).
2. **Food processor:** pulse the onion, coriander and mint about 15 times to a coarse mix (chopped, not a purée). Tip it into a clean tea towel and **squeeze out as much liquid as you can**. Wet mix makes kebabs that break.
3. **Big bowl:** mince, squeezed onion mix, butter, garlic, ginger, ground seeds, garam masala, pepper, paprika, salt and lemon. Knead hard with your hands (or the processor's dough blade) for **3–4 min**, until it looks stringy and sticks together as one mass.
4. Cover and **chill 30 min** (up to overnight). Fry a teaspoon of the mix in a dry pan for 1 min and taste for salt.
5. **Oven 220 °C.** With wet or oiled hands, shape **18 logs** of about 70 g, 12–13 cm long, around skewers if you have them (or just logs). Lay them on 2 parchment-lined trays with a gap between each and brush with the oil.
6. Bake **10 min**, turn, then **5 min** more. Switch to the grill (broiler) on high for **2–3 min** for colour. They're done at 71 °C in the middle, with no pink and clear juices. Air fryer instead: 200 °C, **5 min, turn, 4 min**, in batches.


**Convert to a moist component:** after the meat is fully cooked, remove skewers and cut it into 1–2 cm pieces. In a wide pot simmer the additional **600 g crushed tomatoes + 250 ml water + 1 stock cube** for 10 min. Fold in all the cooked meat and cooking juices and simmer 5 min more, until evenly coated. Fully cook any egg-bound mixture before this step. Divide the meat and sauce evenly into cube molds.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **6 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Burner 1, potatoes:** into a big pot, cover with cold water, add 1 tsp salt, bring to the boil and simmer **15–20 min**, until a knife slides in easily. (Or pressure cooker, **8 min**.) Drain, steam dry in the hot pot for 2 min, then mash with the butter, warm milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper, using a masher, never the food processor (it goes gluey).
2. **Burner 2, wide pot, medium heat** (while the potatoes cook): oil, onion, carrots, celery and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until the onion is soft with no raw bite. Add the mushrooms for **4 min**, until their liquid has cooked off.
3. Turn up to medium-high, add the **beef** and break it up for **6–8 min**, until no pink is left. Add the garlic for 1 min.
4. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 min, then sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 min so there are no dry patches.
5. Pour in the **450 ml stock**, soy sauce, thyme and bay, scraping the bottom. Bring to a simmer, lid half on, **20 min**, stirring now and then.
6. Add the peas and corn for **3 min**. Fish out the bay, add the lemon juice, and taste for salt and pepper. It should be a **thick gravy that holds a trail** when you drag a spoon through, not a soup; if it's thin, simmer with the lid off for 5 min.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices. For assembly, keep the cooked filling and mash separate instead of layering a large pie. - Lentilles corail dissolve into the sauce. If only brown/green adas are available, cook them separately until soft before adding, then blend or mash if a smooth texture is needed; the same dry weight will have a different cooking time.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot on medium-low:** oil and onions with a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft and golden with no raw bite. Add the garlic for 1 min.
2. Stir in the cumin, turmeric and pepper for **30 s** (low heat, so the spices don't scorch), then the tomato paste for 1 min.
3. Add the lentils, carrots, potato, bay leaves, stock cubes and **3.3 L water**. Bring to the boil, stirring the bottom (red lentils catch).
4. Slide in the **whole chicken breasts** and simmer gently, lid ajar, **18 min**. Lift them out onto a board to cool a little.
5. Keep the soup simmering another **12–15 min** (about 30 min in all), stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed and the carrots crush easily.
6. Take out the bay leaves. **Blend until smooth** with a stick blender, or in a blender in batches filled no more than half, lid vented and a towel on top.
7. Shred the chicken with two forks and stir it back in with the lemon juice. Simmer **2 min**, then add the parsley and taste for salt and pepper.
8. Leave it a little thinner than you'd serve it: lentil soups thicken a lot in the freezer.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. 1. **Blend the sauce:** everything in the sauce list into the blender until smooth, **30 s**.

name: Smoky roasted cauliflower and chickpeas
label: SMOKY CAULI
portion: 1/24 of cooked batch; mold count measured at packing
bestWith: protein cubes + rice, pasta, couscous or mash cubes

videos.title: Sriracha Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas Sheet Pan

sections.title: Ingredients (24 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |
|---|---|---|
| Cauliflower (chou-fleur) | 2 medium heads (~2 kg of florets) | bite-sized florets |
| Chickpeas (hommos), canned or home-cooked | ~550 g drained (2 cans + a bit, or 250 g dried, cooked) | rinsed and dried well on a towel |
| Red peppers (felfel ahmar hlou / poivrons rouges) | 3 (~600 g) | 2 cm strips |
| Onions (basal) | 2 (~300 g) | wedges |
| Oil | 3½ tbsp (50 g) | |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tbsp | |
| Smoked paprika (paprika fumé), if you find it | 1 tsp | (or 1 tsp more sweet paprika) |
| Cumin (kammoun), dried oregano, garlic powder (ail en poudre) | 2 tsp, 1 tsp, 1 tsp | |
| Salt, black pepper | 2 tsp, ½ tsp | |
| **Glaze:** honey (asal) | 2 tbsp (40 g) | warmed so it pours |
| Soy sauce (sauce soja) | 1 tbsp (20 ml) | |
| Lemon juice (citron) | 1 tbsp (20 ml) | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 220 °C.** Line 3–4 trays with parchment.
2. Toss the cauliflower, chickpeas, peppers and onion with the oil, spices, salt and pepper in your biggest bowl until everything is red-orange.
3. Spread in **one layer**; crowded trays steam instead of roasting. Roast **20 min**, stirring and swapping the trays round halfway.
4. Whisk the honey, soy and lemon, drizzle it over the trays and toss.
5. Roast **7–8 min** more, until the edges are caramelised and the cauliflower is just tender (it softens again when reheated). Cool on the trays.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **24**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **125 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.content:

3. Whisk all the flour into the cold milk, heat and stir until thick, then cool briefly. Beat the eggs with the cream and seasoning, then stir into the cooled milk sauce. Stir in the cooked filling, grated/crumbled cheese and ready-cooked tuna/cachir if listed. Distribute all solid ingredients evenly.
4. Fill oven-safe cavities no more than three-quarters full. Bake about 20–35 min, depending on cavity size, until the centre is set and reaches 74 °C. A shallow dish can take longer. Rest 5 min, then follow the cooling and cube packing steps; keep the cooked filling soft rather than browning it crisp.

| Oil | 2 tbsp (25 g) | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Toss the chicken with **half** the spice mix.
2. **Big pot, medium-high:** 1 tbsp oil, the chicken for **5 min**, stirring, until white all over. It finishes cooking with the rice. Lift it out into a bowl.
3. Medium heat. The rest of the oil, the onion and peppers for **6 min** until softened. Add the garlic and the rest of the spice mix for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for **1 min**. Pour in the tomatoes and cook **3 min**; this is your cooked salsa.
4. Stir in the rice, the **800 ml stock**, the beans and the corn, then put the chicken back with its juices. Scrape the bottom and bring to a **full boil**.
5. **Lid on, lowest heat, 13 min.** Don't lift the lid. Then heat off and leave it covered **5 min**. The rice should be just tender and the liquid absorbed; if it's still wet, give it 2–3 min uncovered.
6. Fold gently to mix, then stir in the lemon juice and coriander. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

Do not assume grams equal millilitres.

For this rice dish, aim to get the shallow portions into the fridge or freezer within **1 hour**. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Épicerie alternatives: choose a sauce soja suitable for your halal requirements; if unavailable, replace each 15 ml with 15 ml halal stock plus a small pinch of salt and simmer, accepting a less fermented flavour.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Blanch:** boil the carrots and green beans in a big pot of water for **2 min**, drain and spread them out. This makes the stir-fry quick.
2. Whisk the sauce together (soy, honey, vinegar and the cornflour water).
3. **Wok or widest frying pan, high heat, in 3 batches:** 1 tbsp oil, a third of the garlic and ginger for **30 s**, then a third of all the veg (peppers, cabbage, blanched carrots and beans, corn). Stir-fry **4–5 min**, until crisp-tender and a little charred. Pour in a third of the sauce (stir it first) and toss for **1 min**, until glossy and thickened.
4. Tip each batch onto a parchment-lined tray in a thin layer, and scatter the sesame over at the end. Keep the veg a little crisp, because it softens again when reheated.


**Prepare for cubes:** Chop cooked vegetables to 1–2 cm and press gently into the mold. For a loose roasted mixture, mash a spoonful of the vegetables into each portion with a little of its cooking juice to bind it. Reheated cubes will be soft; crisp edges are not the target.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **24**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **125 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the boucherie, ask for the named cut, trimmed and weighed without bone; mince should be hachée devant moi, about 10% fat. Braising cuts need the long cooking method; they are not a direct quick-fry steak substitute.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tsp garam masala, mix ½ tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp black pepper; optional cardamom/clove is only a pinch.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Add the meat and cook, stirring, until fully cooked: poultry 74 °C, beef mince 71 °C.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.
4. Stir in the listed cheese, herbs and lemon juice, if used. Melt the cheese gently into the hot filling. Remove whole spice fragments and divide solids and sauce evenly into molds.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Coulis/passata is pourable tomato, not concentrated paste. If cans or coulis are unavailable, use the same weight of ripe peeled grated tomatoes, then simmer uncovered to the stated sauce consistency before molding; add water only if needed.
- Produce: if batata hlowa is unavailable, replace with equal-weight peeled potato; for a sweeter result use half potato and half carrot, cooked until tender.
- Legume weights in this dish are cooked and drained. Cook dried hommos or loubia separately and weigh the required cooked amount; do not use the listed cooked weight as a dry weight. White beans can replace red beans in the same cooked weight.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; if powders are unavailable, replace 1 tsp garlic powder with 10 g finely crushed garlic and 1 tsp onion powder with 40 g finely grated onion, fully softened and dried in the recipe’s cooking fat before mixing in; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- For the dried-red-bean alternative, soak at least 5 hours, discard the water, boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min, then continue until tender before weighing. Canned beans are already cooked. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:

2. Add the onion and pepper with a pinch of salt for **5 min**, until soft with no raw bite, then the mince, broken up with a wooden spoon, for **6–8 min** until no pink is left. Stir in the garlic, spice mix and salt for **1 min** on low heat so the paprika doesn't scorch.
3. Add the tomatoes, stock and beans. Simmer with the lid on for **12–15 min**, stirring now and then, until a knife slides through the sweet potato but it still holds its shape. If it's wet, **5 min** more with the lid off.
4. **Off the heat:** stir in the fromage rouge and coriander. Taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.
2. Chop vegetables small. Use the listed fat to soften onion/leek for 8–10 min; add garlic for 1 min. Cook mushrooms until their liquid evaporates, spinach until wilted and drained, and grated carrot, pepper or squash until tender. Cook any raw chicken separately in the same pan to 74 °C. Cool the filling briefly.
3. Beat the eggs with the listed milk, cream or fromage blanc and seasoning; stir in any listed flour and breadcrumbs. Stir in the cooked filling, grated/crumbled cheese and ready-cooked tuna/cachir if listed. Distribute all solid ingredients evenly.
4. Fill oven-safe cavities no more than three-quarters full. Bake about 20–35 min, depending on cavity size, until the centre is set and reaches 74 °C. A shallow dish can take longer. Rest 5 min, then follow the cooling and cube packing steps; keep the cooked filling soft rather than browning it crisp.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the finished batch and divide into **8 equal recipe servings**, distributing all ingredients evenly. Use **125 ml food-safe cube molds**. One serving can occupy several cavities; bag the complete set together and label its cube count. Leave the mold’s expansion space.
2. Refrigerate or freeze shallow portions within **2 hours** of cooking/mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**. Freeze in one layer at **−18 °C**; use the freezer’s actual rated capacity. If it is full, refrigerate promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity allows.
3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl and cover loosely. Add 15–30 ml water if the mixture is thick or dry. At 800 W start with 1 min for a small dessert/side cube, or 3 min for a meal serving, then break up and stir. Continue in 30–60 s bursts until the centre reaches **74 °C**. Rest 1 min and check again. Several cubes take longer; temperature determines readiness. Assemble with compatible already frozen cubes. The component is ready to assemble directly from frozen. Do not refreeze reheated food.
