sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Pot 1, high:** 3 L water to a boil. Add the drained split peas and 1 tbsp salt, return to the boil and skim off the foam. **Medium, lid ajar, 15–25 min**: start checking at 15 min. They're ready when they crush easily between your fingers but mostly hold their shape. Green split peas collapse sooner than yellow; if they turn to purée, it's fine, just creamier. Drain.
2. **Pot 2 (wide), medium-high,** while they boil: oil and cumin seeds (they sizzle straight away), then the onions. Cook **6–8 min**, stirring, until golden brown; splash in 2 tbsp water if they catch.
3. Add the garlic and ginger for **2 min**. Turn to low, add the coriander, paprika, turmeric, cumin and 1 tsp salt and stir **1 min**.
4. Add the blended tomatoes, back to medium-high, and cook **3–4 min**, until reduced and the oil shows at the edges. Add the drained split peas and stir-fry **1 min** to coat, then the 500 ml water. Simmer, lid ajar, **10 min**, mashing some of the peas against the side for a creamy texture.
5. **Tarka, small frying pan, medium:** oil and smen; when hot, add the ginger matchsticks for **30 s**, then the coriander until it just wilts (**15 s**). Pour it over the dal and simmer on low **2 min**, until it's thick, moist but not watery, with a sheen of fat on top.
6. Off the heat: lemon juice, garam masala and black pepper. Taste for salt (the peas were boiled in salted water, so go easy).


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Glaze, small pot on a burner, medium:** oil and onion for **5 min** until soft, then the garlic for **1 min**, stirring so it doesn't brown. Add the soy, honey, ketchup, lemon juice, zest, vinegar, paprika and water and **simmer 4 min**. Stir in the cornflour slurry, simmer 1 min until it coats a spoon, and take it off the heat. 2. **Oven 210 °C.** Two trays lined with baking paper, lightly oiled. Season the drumsticks with the salt and pepper, toss them in the larger part of the glaze, and lay them in one layer, not touching.
3. **Bake 20 min**, swapping the trays and turning the drumsticks at 10 min.
4. Brush the reserved glaze over them and **bake 12–15 min more**, until the glaze is sticky and dark at the edges and the thickest drumstick is 74 °C next to the bone (juices clear).
5. **Air fryer instead** (in batches of 6–7): 190 °C, 20 min, turning at 10, glazing for the last 5 min.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **8 L pot on medium-high:** oil and mince for **8 min**, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left. Spoon off any pool of fat (the source insists, and it keeps the soup from going greasy).
2. Add the onions and peppers for **8 min**, stirring, until the onions are soft. Add the garlic for 1 min, then the tomato paste, paprika, marjoram and pepper for 1 min.
3. Add the tomatoes, passata, stock cubes and **1.8 L water**. Bring to the boil, then lid ajar and simmer **20 min**.

6. The rice keeps soaking up broth, so portion it straight away and leave it a little looser than you'd serve it.

- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method.
2. **Oven, 200 °C**, while the beans cook: toss the sweet potato and pepper with 15 ml oil and a pinch of salt on a parchment-lined tray, one layer. Roast **25 min**, turning once, until the sweet potato is tender and browned at the edges.
3. **Big pot, medium-high:** 15 ml oil, onion, carrot and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft. Turn to medium, add the garlic, paprikas, cumin, oregano and cinnamon for **1 min**, then the tomato paste for **2 min**.
4. Add the blended tomatoes, beans, sweetcorn and the 200 ml stock. Simmer with the lid off for **15 min**, stirring now and then.
5. Fold in the roasted sweet potato and pepper and simmer **5 min** more, stirring gently so the cubes stay whole. It should be thick and spoonable; if it's thin, give it 5 min more with the lid off. Off the heat, add the coriander and taste for salt and pepper.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Produce: if batata hlowa is unavailable, replace with equal-weight peeled potato; for a sweeter result use half potato and half carrot, cooked until tender.
- Épicerie alternatives: white sugar replaces cassonade gram for gram in this cooked dish.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.

1. **Pressure cooker:** 250 ml water in the bottom, the chunks on the steamer rack or trivet (above the water, so they don't go watery). **High pressure 8 min**, then quick release. They should be soft enough to crush with a fork. (Or roast them whole in their skins on a tray at 200 °C for **50–60 min** if the oven is on anyway; it tastes a bit richer.)
2. Tip them into a big bowl or back into the empty pot and leave **2 min** to steam off.
3. Mash with the butter, sugar, spices, salt and pepper using a masher or fork. Taste; it should be sweet but still savoury.
4. Spoon the warm mash into cube molds in the measured serving shares, then cool promptly as described below.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

bestWith: rice, pasta or couscous cubes + vegetable cubes

sections.title: Ingredients (7 recipe servings; cube yield measured after cooking)
sections.content:
| Ingredient | Amount | Prep |

| Plain yogurt (yaourt nature) | 1½ pots (~180 g) | |
| Lemon juice (citron) | 2 tbsp (30 ml) | |
| Oil (olive or table) | 1½ tbsp (20 ml) | plus a little for the trays |
| Sweet paprika (paprika doux) | 1 tbsp (7 g) | |
| Mild curry powder (curry doux) | 1 tsp | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: yaourt nature must be unsweetened; brassé describes texture and does not guarantee Greek-yogurt protein.
- Seasoning alternatives: for 1 tbsp curry doux, use 1 tsp each ground coriander, cumin and turmeric; use sweet paprika separately where listed.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Marinate:** mix everything except the chicken in a big bowl, then work it into the slashes. Cover and fridge for **4 h to overnight** (not longer, or the yogurt turns it mushy).
2. **Oven 230 °C**, two trays lined with foil and lightly oiled. Lay the thighs out flat in one layer, not touching, shaking off the thick excess marinade.
3. Roast on the top two shelves for **20–22 min**, swapping the trays at 10 min, until charred at the edges and the juices run clear when you cut into the thickest one (74 °C inside). If you want more char, 2–3 min under the grill at the end.
4. Rest **5 min**, then cut each thigh into 3–4 cm bites. Spoon any tray juices over.
5. **Air fryer instead:** 190 °C, in batches of 5–6 thighs, **14–16 min**, turning at 8.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **7**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

- Seasoning alternatives: plain paprika doux replaces sweet smoked paprika in the same amount; use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Before the dish:** soak red kidney beans at least 5 hours (overnight in the fridge is practical), discard the soaking water, and boil briskly in fresh water for at least 30 min. Continue until fully tender and drain. Use these already-cooked beans in the recipe; skip any later pressure step whose sole purpose is cooking beans, and add the beans after other meat is tender. Never put merely soaked kidney beans in a slow cooker. [FDA bean guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/chemical-contaminants-pesticides/natural-toxins-food).


**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. Cook and drain all listed dried legumes separately until tender, using the kidney-bean preparation above for red beans; other legumes can follow their pressure-cooker or packet method. Keep 150 ml bean cooking water.
2. **Big pot, medium-high** (or the rinsed pressure cooker on sauté): oil, onion, carrot and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft. Add the pepper and zucchini for **3 min**.
3. Turn to medium, add the garlic and all the dry spices, stir **1 min** so they bloom without burning, then the tomato paste for **2 min**, stirring so it darkens a little.
4. Add the blended tomatoes, beans, sweetcorn, crumbled stock cube and the 150 ml bean water. Scrape the bottom well.
5. Simmer with the lid off for **20–25 min**, stirring every 5 min. Crush a ladle of beans against the side of the pot for body. It's done when it's thick enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a clear line for a second.
6. Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander. Taste for salt.

| Tomato paste (concentré de tomate) | 50 g (2 tbsp) | |

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

- Use the specified fine or coarse boulgour. For a cooked spoonable grain mixture, the same dry weight of frik is an alternative: simmer separately until tender and drain excess water before mixing, rather than just soaking it as for fine bulgur.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Big pot, medium:** butter and olive oil, then the onions for **8 min**, until soft and lightly golden.
2. Add the grated tomatoes and cook **5 min**, stirring.
3. Add the bulgur and stir for 1 min to coat it. Add salt, pepper, cumin and paprika, then the tomato paste, and stir again.
4. Pour in the **1.6 L boiling stock**, bring back to the boil, then lid on and a low simmer for **12–15 min**, until the liquid has been absorbed and the bulgur is tender with a little bite. If it dries out before it's tender, add a splash of boiling water.
5. Off the heat, lid on, rest **10 min**. Fluff with a fork and taste for salt.
6. **Spread it thin on 2 parchment-lined trays straight away** and let it steam off for 15 min.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Dice onion, garlic and other vegetables finely; cut chicken to 1–2 cm or break mince into small pieces. Drain canned ingredients and grate the cheese. Mix the listed dried seasonings, using only mild spices.
2. Heat the listed cooking fat in a wide pot. Cook onion and firm vegetables for 8–10 min until soft; cook garlic and spices for 1 min. Cook the chopped ready-cooked cachir with the vegetables until heated through.
3. Add the listed tomato/paste, cooked beans, sweetcorn, condiments and other filling ingredients; keep cheese and finishing herbs/lemon aside. Add 150–250 ml water as needed and simmer 10–15 min, until vegetables are tender and the mixture is moist and spoonable, not dry crumbles. Fold spinach in for the last 5 min.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Heat the oven to 170 °C. Use silicone cube molds explicitly rated for baking, supported on a tray; freezer-only plastic molds must not go in the oven. Alternatively bake in a shallow lined dish, then portion the cooked filling into freezer molds.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Pot:** potatoes in cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook **10–12 min**, until tender but still holding their shape. Drain well and spread out to steam dry for 5 min. Wet potatoes make a soggy tajine.
2. **Frying pan, medium heat:** the 2 tbsp tuna oil and the onion for **10 min**, until soft and lightly golden. Add the garlic for **1 min**, then take it off the heat.
3. **Oven 180 °C.** Oil a **30 × 40 cm** deep oven tray and line the base with parchment.
4. In your biggest bowl, gently mix the potatoes, onion, flaked tuna, parsley, grated cheese, cheese-triangle pieces and olives.
5. Whisk the eggs with the turmeric, tabel, salt and pepper, just until combined. Pour over the filling and fold gently without crushing the potatoes. Tip into the tray and level it without pressing.
6. Bake **30–35 min** (longer than in the source, because the tray is deeper), until the middle is set and a knife comes out with no liquid egg, and the top is golden.
7. Rest **15 min**, then cut into **15 squares** (3 × 5).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. Cook the rice separately until just tender. Work on the filling while it cooks, then combine promptly; get the finished shallow portions into refrigeration or freezing within 1 hour of the rice finishing.
2. Finely chop all onion and garlic. Dice cabbage, peppers or zucchini to 1–2 cm as listed; there is no stuffing or rolling.
3. In the oil, soften all onion for 8 min. Add garlic and beef mince, breaking it up, and cook until the mince reaches 71 °C. Add seasoning and any listed tomato/paste for 2 min.
4. Add the diced vegetables, stock cube dissolved in 400 ml water, and cooked drained chickpeas. Cover and simmer 15–25 min until vegetables are tender, adding water if needed. Reduce uncovered to a thick, moist stew.
5. Fold in cooked rice, herbs and lemon if listed. Heat through and divide evenly into molds. The mixture contains both protein and starch; no egg binder is needed.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven to 180 °C.** Line a 20 × 30 cm baking tray with baking paper, leaving some overhang on the long sides so you can lift the slab out.
2. **Brown the butter**, one burner, medium heat, in a light-coloured saucepan: melt it and keep stirring for **5–7 min**. It foams, then the solids sink and turn deep golden-brown and it smells nutty. Take it off the heat straight away (it goes from brown to burnt in seconds).
3. Put both sugars in a large bowl, pour the hot butter over and **whisk 1 min** until smooth. Leave it 5 min so it's warm, not hot.
4. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla sugar, until glossy.
5. In another bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Fold them into the wet mix with a spatula until no dry flour shows. Don't beat it; over-mixing makes them cakey.
6. Fold in most of the white chocolate and peanuts, spread the batter evenly in the tray, and scatter the rest on top.
7. **Bake 25–30 min**, until the edges are golden and a knife in the centre comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter. They firm up as they cool.
8. Cool in the tray for **15 min**, lift the slab out on its paper and cool on a rack for another 30 min. Cut into **15 bars** (3 × 5).


**Cube version:** use the completed baked mixture, including any listed glaze, after it has set. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven to 180 °C.** Oil three loaf tins (~25 cm) and line the bases with baking paper.
2. **Veg**, one burner, medium-high, in a large frying pan: 1 tsp oil and the courgettes with a pinch of salt for **6–8 min**, until tender and all their water has cooked off (wet courgettes make a soggy cake). Add the garlic for the last minute. Tip into a bowl to cool. In the same pan, cook the diced peppers for **8–10 min** until soft and catching at the edges. Tip into a second bowl.
3. **Batter:** whisk the eggs, milk and olive oil in a large bowl. Mix the flour, baking powder, pepper and pinch of salt separately, then whisk them into the eggs in three goes, just until smooth (a few lumps are fine). Stir in the grated gouda.
4. **Divide the batter** between three bowls, about **435 g each**.
5. Fold the fillings in gently, one per bowl: **A** courgettes, feta and mint; **B** peppers, olives and camembert; **C** sun-dried tomatoes, basil and feta. (Tossing the diced cheese and veg in a spoon of flour first stops them sinking.)
6. Pour into the tins; scatter the sunflower seeds over loaf C. Mark each tin (a strip of paper under the edge) so you know which is which later.
7. **Bake all three together 40–45 min**, until risen, golden and a knife in the middle comes out clean.
8. Cool in the tins **10 min**, turn out onto a rack and cool **30 min** more. Cut each loaf into **10 slices** (~2.5 cm).

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions
sections.content:
- At the volailler, specify boneless, skinless edible weight. Ask for poultry minced fresh if needed; do not replace the same weight with bone-in pieces or cachir.
- Dairy: fromage rouge means gouda/edam-style block cheese for grating, not spreadable triangles.
- Produce: washed chopped blettes can replace spinach by trimmed weight; cook chopped stalks with the onions before adding the leaves; use local krafs stems by weight; with a very leafy bunch use a few leaves for flavour and make up the missing stem weight with carrot.
- Buy dried legumes at the épicerie; soak overnight in the fridge in hot weather, discard that water and cook until fully tender. Keep legumes and liquid below the pressure cooker half-full mark. Older beans may need longer; acidic tomato sauce is added after they soften.
- Seasoning alternatives: use plain dried thyme if oregano is unavailable; zaâtar here means the herb, not a salted sesame blend.
- Épicerie alternatives: check bouillon and processed meats are halal; mild fresh chicken sausage is different from cooked cachir.
- The calculation covers the main ingredient list. Alternatives change nutrition and cost; figures are ingredient estimates, not a guarantee for every local brand. There is no grocery budget cap.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Beans, pressure cooker:** cover the soaked beans with fresh water by 3 cm, **high pressure 12 min**, natural release. (Unsoaked: 35 min.) They should be soft right through. Drain and keep aside.
2. **Burner 1, big wide pot, medium heat:** 2 tbsp oil, the onion, celery and a pinch of salt for **8 min**, until soft with no raw bite. Add the carrot and courgette and cook **5 min**, then the garlic for 1 min.
3. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 min, then the grated tomatoes, stock, coriander, oregano, pepper and salt. Simmer with the lid off for **25 min**, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are very soft and the sauce has thickened.
4. **Burner 2, pot of salted water:** cook the pasta for **3 min less than the packet says**. Drain.
5. **Burner 3, small pan, medium-high** (while the sauce simmers): the last tbsp of oil, then the chicken with a pinch of salt and pepper, **6–7 min**, turning, until white all through with no pink. Add it to the sauce.
6. Stir the beans, spinach and **half the cheese** into the sauce for **3 min**, until the spinach has wilted. Tip in the pasta and stir well; it should look **saucier than you'd serve it**, as the pasta keeps drinking as it cools. Stir in the basil and taste for salt.


**Prepare for cubes:** For molding, cut cooked meat, meatballs, sausage and vegetables to at most 1–2 cm. Stir solids and sauce together before dividing so every serving gets its share. Add only enough hot water to make a dry mixture spoonable; keep cooking juices.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **6**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

sections.title: Local supplies and substitutions

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Widest heavy pot with a lid, medium-high:** oil, onion, carrot and celery for **5 min**, until just tender. Add the zucchini, garlic, turmeric, pepper and salt for **1 min**.
2. Add the drained rice and stir for **2 min**, until every grain is coated and smells toasty.
3. Pour in the **1.25 L hot stock**, bring to a rolling boil, then put the lid on and turn the heat to the lowest setting for **15 min**. Don't lift the lid.
4. Check: the top should have little steam holes and no liquid should pool when you push the rice aside with a fork. If there's liquid, give it 2–3 min more. Off the heat, lid on, rest **10 min**.
5. Fork it through gently, folding in the dill, parsley and lemon juice. **Spread it on 2 trays straight away** so it stops cooking and steams off for 5–10 min.
6. While it's still warm, press it firmly into the silicone muffin trays, about 105 g per well, 20 wells.

sections.title: Freeze
sections.content:
1. Weigh the cooked batch (without the pot) and divide by **10**. That weight is one recipe serving. Distribute meat, sauce and vegetables evenly. Use **250 ml food-safe cube molds**, leaving the maker's expansion space. A serving may occupy more than one cavity; bag all its cubes together, including any smaller final cube. Do not assume grams equal millilitres.
2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of cooking, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. For this rice dish, aim to get the shallow portions into the fridge or freezer within **1 hour**. Freeze in a single layer at **−18 °C** until solid. If the freezer has no capacity, chill promptly at **4 °C or below** and freeze as soon as capacity is available.
3. Unmold and bag by component or serving. Label the dish, date and **number of cubes per recipe serving**. Vacuum-seal only once solid. Use within one month for this system. See [the cube packing guide](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Reheat
sections.content: **Microwave from frozen:** place the labeled serving of cubes in a microwave-safe bowl. Add 15–30 ml water to rice, pasta or thick sauce, and cover loosely. At **800 W**, start with **3 min**, break up and stir, then heat in **1 min bursts**, stirring between each, until the centre of every component reaches **74 °C**. Rest **1 min** and check again. A mixed bowl or several cubes takes longer; use temperature, not a fixed total time. Add fragile cream sauces in shorter bursts once loosened. No prior defrosting or fresh garnish is required. Reheat only what you will eat; do not refreeze reheated food.

**Pressure cooker:** use the manufacturer’s minimum thin-liquid volume and fill limits (at most half full for beans, grains and foaming food). Times start at full pressure. On a stovetop cocotte, sauté with the lid off on the burner; an electric sauté button is not required. Add thick dairy/flour sauces after pressure cooking where possible, then reduce uncovered.


1. **Chickpeas, pressure cooker:** drained soaked chickpeas, fresh water to 3 cm above, **no more than half full**. **High pressure 15 min**, natural release 15 min. They should squash easily between two fingers. Drain.

4. In a bowl, whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot liquid until smooth (added straight in, it clumps), then stir it into the pot. Add the spinach and simmer with the lid off **5 min**, stirring often: peanut sauce catches on the bottom quickly.
5. It should be a thick, creamy stew. Off the heat, add the lemon juice and coriander and taste for salt.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:

2. Stir the plain yogurt, honey and vanilla sugar together. Warm the peanut butter briefly so it stirs easily, then fold it in with the fruit and chopped peanuts.
3. Melt the chocolate in 20 s microwave bursts, stirring between them. Ripple it through the yogurt mixture so every portion contains some.
4. Divide evenly into **125 ml cube molds** and freeze promptly. Keep these as cold dessert cubes rather than a hot meal ingredient.

sections.content:

2. Portion promptly into shallow molds. Refrigerate or freeze within **2 hours** of mixing, or **1 hour above 32 °C**; do not wait for a whole pot to cool. sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Oven 175 °C.** Line two 25 cm loaf tins (moules à cake) with parchment.
2. In a big bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate, spices and salt.
3. In a second bowl, whisk the oil, both sugars, eggs, vanilla sugar, lemon zest and juice until smooth. Stir in the zucchini with all its juice.
4. Fold the wet into the dry **just until combined**, then fold in the chocolate.
5. Split between the tins, level, and scatter the oats on top.
6. Bake **50–55 min**, until risen, golden and a skewer in the middle comes out clean (a smear of melted chocolate is fine). Cover loosely with foil for the last 15 min if the tops brown too fast.
7. Rest 10–15 min, then remove from the tins and portion into smaller pieces. Chill promptly on a shallow tray if not ready to mold; do not wait an hour on the counter in a hot kitchen.

Cut into pieces smaller than a mold cavity and press gently into 60 ml freezer molds; use the listed moist fruit/filling to bind crumbs, not raw batter. Pack separate flavours separately. A cake cube is a dessert component; serve it warm with a separately frozen fruit or yogurt component.

3. Once solid, unmold into labeled zip bags; vacuum-seal only frozen cubes. Use within one month. See [cube packing](../../docs/packing.md).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
1. **Biggest pot (8 L if you have it), high heat:** oil and onions for **8–10 min**, until lightly golden.
2. Turn to medium. Add the garlic, ginger and cumin seeds for **1 min**, until the raw smell has gone. Add the tomato, salt, ground coriander, pepper and paprika and cook **1 min**.
3. Pile in the zucchini with 60 ml water and stir to coat; it looks like far too much, but it collapses within 10 min. Lid on, **10 min** on medium, stirring once.
4. Once most of the water has gone, break the zucchini up with a wooden spoon. Stir in the turmeric.
5. Lid on, lowest heat, **20 min**, stirring halfway (add a splash of water only if it catches).
6. **Lid off, high heat for 5–10 min**, stirring, until every bit of liquid has gone and the oil glistens at the edges. Stir in the fresh coriander and taste for salt. Cool **30 min**.
